points.en: Of the three products, phosphate needs no further degradation because free phosphate serves as a buffer salt in its own right.

points.zh: 核糖一般也不需要再降解：细胞要造新核苷酸就直接经磷酸戊糖途径拿去构筑，不要的话也可以转成葡萄糖。
points.en: Ribose too usually needs no further degradation: if the cell is building new nucleotides it feeds straight through the pentose phosphate pathway, and if not it can be converted to glucose.

extra.zh: 磷酸二酯酶的产物不是碱基，是单核苷酸 —— 碱基、核糖、磷酸三部分都还在。证据就在他自己的下一句：这个所谓的「碱基」还要被磷酸单酯酶切掉磷酸、再被核苷酶切掉碱基；只有核苷酸才有磷酸可切，游离碱基上什么都没有。核酸酶和磷酸二酯酶动的是骨架上的磷酸二酯键，产物必然是单核苷酸。
extra.en: The products of phosphodiesterase are not bases but mononucleotides — base, ribose and phosphate all still present. His own next sentence is the proof: these so-called bases then have phosphate removed by a phosphomonoesterase and the base removed by a nucleosidase. Only a nucleotide has a phosphate to remove; a free base has nothing. Nucleases and phosphodiesterases attack backbone phosphodiester bonds, so mononucleotides are the necessary product.

extra.zh: 「三步降解」是口误，他在约 00:52:29 当场自纠为「一共是经过两步」，以两步为准：核苷酸 →（核苷酸酶／磷酸单酯酶，脱磷酸）→ 核苷 →（核苷酶／核苷磷酸化酶，断 N-糖苷键）→ 碱基 + 糖。如果把前面磷酸二酯酶那一刀也算上，从长链到三组分一共是三刀，这大概是他一开始数成三步的来源。
extra.en: 'Three steps' was a slip he corrected on the spot around 00:52:29 to 'two steps in all'. Take two: nucleotide → (nucleotidase / phosphomonoesterase, dephosphorylation) → nucleoside → (nucleosidase / nucleoside phosphorylase, N-glycosidic cleavage) → base + sugar. Counting the earlier phosphodiesterase cut as well gives three cuts from long chain to three components, which is probably where the initial three came from.

extra.zh: 「核苷磷酸酶」应为核苷磷酸化酶 nucleoside phosphorylase（嘌呤那一支就是 PNP）。它做的不是水解而是磷酸解 phosphorolysis：核苷 + Pi → 碱基 + 核糖-1-磷酸。所以糖上带磷酸 —— 他先说产物是「碱基加戊糖」，后又补「是带磷酸的核糖」，两句自相矛盾，后一句才对。磷酸酶 phosphatase 是脱磷酸的酶，与这一步方向正好相反，名字不能混。植物和微生物那条路用的是核苷水解酶 nucleoside hydrolase，产物才是碱基 + 游离核糖，这一点他讲对了。
extra.en: 'Nucleoside phosphatase' should be nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP on the purine branch). It performs not hydrolysis but phosphorolysis: nucleoside + Pi → base + ribose-1-phosphate, which is why the sugar carries a phosphate. He first said the products were base plus pentose and then added that the ribose bears phosphate; the two statements contradict, and the second is right. A phosphatase removes phosphate, the opposite direction, so the names must not be swapped. The plant and microbial route uses nucleoside hydrolase, and there the products really are base plus free ribose — that part he got right.

extra.zh: 「核糖通过糖异生变成葡萄糖」说得太松，方向不错但路径名用混了。降解得到的核糖先被核糖激酶磷酸化成 5-磷酸核糖，经磷酸戊糖途径的非氧化段（转酮酶、转醛酶）重排成 6-磷酸果糖和 3-磷酸甘油醛，才汇入糖酵解／糖异生的主干。糖异生本身是从丙酮酸、乳酸、甘油和生糖氨基酸起步的另一套酶，不接收五碳糖。
extra.en: 'Ribose becomes glucose via gluconeogenesis' is loose — the direction is right but the pathway is misnamed. Ribose from degradation is first phosphorylated by ribokinase to ribose-5-phosphate, then rearranged through the non-oxidative arm of the pentose phosphate pathway (transketolase, transaldolase) into fructose-6-phosphate and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate, and only then joins the glycolytic/gluconeogenic trunk. Gluconeogenesis proper is a separate enzyme set starting from pyruvate, lactate, glycerol and glucogenic amino acids, and does not take pentoses.

quiz.q_zh: 核苷磷酸化酶催化核苷降解，产物是什么？
quiz.q_en: What are the products when nucleoside phosphorylase degrades a nucleoside?

options.zh: 游离碱基和一分子 5-磷酸核糖
options.en: A free base and one molecule of ribose-5-phosphate

options.zh: 游离的碱基和一分子完全游离的核糖
options.en: A free base and one molecule of completely free ribose

options.zh: 游离碱基和一分子核糖-1-磷酸
options.en: A free base and one molecule of ribose-1-phosphate

options.zh: 单核苷酸和一分子游离的无机磷酸
options.en: A mononucleotide and a molecule of inorganic phosphate

quiz.explain_zh: 这一步是磷酸解：核苷 + Pi → 碱基 + 核糖-1-磷酸，磷酸接在原来连碱基的 C1' 上。产生完全游离核糖的是植物和微生物用的核苷水解酶，不是磷酸化酶；产生单核苷酸的是上一步磷酸二酯酶切链；5-磷酸核糖是核糖-1-磷酸经磷酸核糖变位酶转位之后才得到的下一站产物。
quiz.explain_en: This step is phosphorolysis: nucleoside + Pi → base + ribose-1-phosphate, with the phosphate landing on C1' where the base used to be. Fully free ribose comes from nucleoside hydrolase in plants and microbes, not from the phosphorylase; mononucleotides come from the earlier phosphodiesterase cut; and ribose-5-phosphate arises only afterwards, once phosphoribomutase shifts the phosphate.

quiz.q_zh: 他先说三步、后改口两步，被保留下来的那两步指的是什么？
quiz.q_en: He said three steps then corrected to two — which two steps did he keep?

options.zh: 磷酸二酯酶切链，核苷磷酸化酶断开糖苷键
options.en: Phosphodiesterase cuts the chain, then phosphorylase breaks the glycoside

options.zh: 磷酸单酯酶脱磷酸，核苷酶断开 N-糖苷键
options.en: Phosphomonoesterase removes phosphate, nucleosidase cuts the glycoside

options.zh: 核蛋白变性释放核酸，磷酸二酯酶切开长链
options.en: Nucleoprotein denatured to free the chain, then phosphodiesterase cuts

options.zh: 核苷酸脱氨生成次黄嘌呤，再氧化成为尿酸
options.en: The nucleotide is deaminated to hypoxanthine, then oxidised to urate

quiz.explain_zh: 他数的这两步都发生在单核苷酸之后：先脱磷酸得到核苷，再断糖苷键得到碱基和糖。核蛋白变性是消化的准备步骤，不在这两步之内；脱氨和氧化成尿酸是后面碱基降解的内容，与拆解组分无关；把磷酸二酯酶那一刀和糖苷键那一刀凑成一对则跳掉了中间脱磷酸的必经步骤。
quiz.explain_en: Both steps he counted come after the mononucleotide: dephosphorylation to the nucleoside, then glycosidic cleavage to base plus sugar. Denaturing nucleoprotein is preparatory digestion and not one of the two; deamination and oxidation to urate belong to the later base degradation, not to taking the nucleotide apart; and pairing the phosphodiester cut with the glycosidic cut skips the obligatory dephosphorylation in between.

quiz.q_zh: 植物和一些微生物在核苷这一步与人体的差别是什么？
quiz.q_en: How does the nucleoside step differ in plants and some microbes from ours?

options.zh: 用核苷激酶磷酸化，得到核苷酸再进一步降解
options.en: A nucleoside kinase phosphorylates it to a nucleotide first

options.zh: 用核苷氧化酶氧化，直接得到尿酸和戊糖
options.en: A nucleoside oxidase oxidises it straight to urate and pentose

options.zh: 用核苷脱氨酶脱氨，得到肌苷再断开糖苷键
options.en: A nucleoside deaminase gives inosine before glycosidic cleavage

options.zh: 用核苷水解酶水解，得到碱基和游离核糖
options.en: A nucleoside hydrolase gives the free base and free ribose

quiz.explain_zh: 老师说的正是这一条：植物和一些微生物把核苷彻底水解，糖以游离核糖的形式出来，而我们走磷酸解、糖带着一个磷酸出来。核苷激酶做的是补救途径的磷酸化，方向相反；核苷层面没有直接氧化成尿酸的酶，尿酸是碱基氧化的终点；核苷脱氨酶（如腺苷脱氨酶）确实存在，但那是脱氨反应，与这里比较的糖苷键断裂方式不是一回事。
quiz.explain_en: This is exactly his point: plants and some microbes hydrolyse the nucleoside completely and the sugar leaves as free ribose, whereas we use phosphorolysis and the sugar leaves carrying a phosphate. Nucleoside kinase phosphorylates in the salvage direction, the opposite way; no nucleoside-level enzyme oxidises straight to urate, which is the endpoint of base oxidation; and nucleoside deaminases such as adenosine deaminase do exist but perform deamination, a different reaction from the glycosidic cleavage being compared here.

title_zh: 为什么必须降解碱基；嘌呤脱氨：A→次黄嘌呤，G→黄嘌呤
title_en: Why the base must be degraded; purine deamination: A to hypoxanthine, G to xanthine

points.zh: 他给出必须降解碱基的理由：碱基里实际上带有大量的氨，碱基上面有很多氨基。
points.en: His reason why the base must be degraded: bases in fact carry a great deal of nitrogen, with many amino groups on them.

points.zh: 他接着说，如果放任碱基在体内大量堆积，某种程度上也会导致氨中毒的现象发生。
points.en: He went on to say that letting bases accumulate in quantity would to some degree cause ammonia toxicity.

points.zh: 结论：核苷酸代谢这一章主要关心的就是碱基的降解，磷酸和核糖都不用管。
points.en: His conclusion: this chapter is chiefly about base degradation; neither phosphate nor ribose needs attention.

points.zh: 碱基降解分两大部分 —— 嘌呤和嘧啶，两者路径完全不同，先讲嘌呤。
points.en: Base degradation splits into two halves, purines and pyrimidines, with entirely different routes; purines first.

points.zh: 他只要求记住酶产物，不要求记酶名：腺嘌呤上那个位置如果是氨基，这个东西就叫腺嘌呤。
points.en: He asked for the products rather than the enzyme names: if that position bears an amino group, the compound is adenine.

points.zh: 腺嘌呤在腺嘌呤脱氨酶作用下先脱氨，产物叫次黄嘌呤 hypoxanthine。
points.en: Adenine is first deaminated by adenine deaminase to give hypoxanthine.

points.zh: 他把次黄嘌呤和上一章的转氨联合脱氨挂钩，说这个步骤是可逆的，因此也能一定程度上承担转氨基的作用，「联合脱氨就是在这来的」。
points.en: He linked hypoxanthine back to the coupled transamination-deamination of the previous chapter, saying this step is reversible and can therefore partly serve as transamination, 'which is where coupled deamination comes from'.

points.zh: 鸟嘌呤对应地在鸟嘌呤脱氨酶作用下脱氨，产物是黄嘌呤 xanthine。
points.en: Guanine correspondingly is deaminated by guanine deaminase to xanthine.

points.zh: 讲到这里他自己也把次黄嘌呤和黄嘌呤搞混了，中断讲课要求把 A、T、C、G、U 的结构图贴到旁边对照着讲。
points.en: At this point he muddled hypoxanthine and xanthine himself, paused, and asked for a structure chart of A, T, C, G and U to be pasted alongside for reference.

extra.zh: 「碱基堆积会导致氨中毒」不准确，而且会把后面痛风那一段的逻辑带偏。嘌呤碱基的分解终产物是尿酸 uric acid，嘌呤上的氮最后是以尿酸的形式排出去的，堆积引起的是高尿酸血症和痛风 —— 他自己在约 00:59:34 讲痛风时用的正是这个逻辑。只有嘧啶降解才开环释放 NH3 和 CO2，那部分氮确实要进尿素循环，但用「氨中毒」概括整个碱基降解的意义是错的。
extra.en: 'Accumulating bases cause ammonia toxicity' is inaccurate and skews the logic of the gout section that follows. The end product of purine base degradation is uric acid, and purine nitrogen leaves the body as urate; accumulation gives hyperuricaemia and gout — the very logic he uses himself around 00:59:34. Only pyrimidine degradation opens the ring and releases NH3 and CO2, and that nitrogen does enter the urea cycle, but summarising the purpose of base degradation as avoiding ammonia toxicity is wrong.

extra.zh: 「这个步骤它是可逆的」不成立，而且这个前提被他带进了下一段。水解脱氨（腺嘌呤／腺苷／AMP → 次黄嘌呤／肌苷／IMP）放出的是游离 NH3，反应实际上不可逆，也根本不是转氨反应 —— 转氨是氨基在氨基酸和 α-酮酸之间对调，不放游离氨。由 IMP 做回 AMP 走的是完全另一条路：腺苷酸代琥珀酸合成酶（IMP + 天冬氨酸 + GTP）加裂解酶两步，氨基来自天冬氨酸，而不是把刚脱掉的那个氨再加回去。
extra.en: 'This step is reversible' does not hold, and he carries the premise into the next stretch. Hydrolytic deamination (adenine/adenosine/AMP → hypoxanthine/inosine/IMP) releases free NH3 and is effectively irreversible, and it is not transamination at all — transamination swaps an amino group between an amino acid and a keto acid without freeing ammonia. Rebuilding AMP from IMP takes a different route entirely: adenylosuccinate synthetase (IMP + aspartate + GTP) then a lyase, with the amino group coming from aspartate rather than from the ammonia just removed.

extra.zh: 嘌呤核苷酸循环 purine nucleotide cycle 确实存在，以骨骼肌为主，但它是 IMP → 腺苷酸代琥珀酸 → AMP →（AMP 脱氨酶）→ IMP 三个酶组成的循环，中间物是 IMP 这个核苷酸，不是游离碱基次黄嘌呤。而教科书里的「联合脱氨基作用」通常指转氨基 + 谷氨酸脱氢酶氧化脱氨的偶联，主要在肝和肾。两套机制名字接近、器官不同、中间物层级也不同，别混成一个。
extra.en: The purine nucleotide cycle is real and runs mainly in skeletal muscle, but it is a three-enzyme loop IMP → adenylosuccinate → AMP → (AMP deaminase) → IMP, whose intermediate is the nucleotide IMP, not the free base hypoxanthine. Textbook 'coupled deamination', meanwhile, means transamination coupled to oxidative deamination by glutamate dehydrogenase, mainly in liver and kidney. Similar names, different organs, different structural level — do not merge them.

extra.zh: 层级问题：化学上「腺嘌呤脱氨变次黄嘌呤」没错（6 位氨基水解成 6-羟基），但人体内的脱氨主要发生在核苷／核苷酸层次 —— 腺苷脱氨酶 ADA 催化腺苷→肌苷，AMP 脱氨酶催化 AMP→IMP；作用于游离腺嘌呤的脱氨酶主要见于微生物。临床落点也在这里：ADA 缺陷导致 dATP 蓄积毒害淋巴细胞，就是重症联合免疫缺陷 SCID，也是最早做基因治疗的病之一。老师在约 01:00:06 之后自己会讲到三个水平，这一条正好接得上。
extra.en: A level issue: chemically 'adenine deaminates to hypoxanthine' is fine (the 6-amino hydrolyses to 6-oxo), but in humans deamination happens mainly at the nucleoside and nucleotide level — adenosine deaminase (ADA) converts adenosine to inosine, AMP deaminase converts AMP to IMP; deaminases acting on free adenine are mostly microbial. The clinical anchor sits here too: ADA deficiency lets dATP accumulate and poison lymphocytes, giving severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID), one of the first diseases treated by gene therapy. He himself gets to the three levels after about 01:00:06, where this joins up.

quiz.q_zh: 嘌呤碱基大量分解在人体内真正造成的问题是什么？
quiz.q_en: What problem does heavy purine base degradation actually cause in humans?

options.zh: 游离氨大量释放，引起氨中毒和肝性脑病
options.en: Free ammonia release causing ammonia toxicity and encephalopathy

options.zh: 腺嘌呤原样沉积在关节滑膜形成针状结晶
options.en: Adenine deposits unchanged in the synovium as needle crystals

options.zh: 尿酸生成过多，引起高尿酸血症和痛风
options.en: Overproduction of uric acid causing hyperuricaemia and gout

options.zh: 次黄嘌呤在血中蓄积，抑制线粒体呼吸链
options.en: Hypoxanthine accumulates in blood and inhibits respiration

quiz.explain_zh: 嘌呤的氮最终被封装在尿酸这个环里排出，人又缺尿酸氧化酶，代谢就停在尿酸，溶解度低就析出尿酸钠结晶引起痛风 —— 老师后面讲海鲜汤时用的正是这个逻辑。他这里说的氨中毒不对：嘌呤降解不以游离氨为终产物，释放 NH3 的是嘧啶那一支。关节里析出的是尿酸钠而不是腺嘌呤；次黄嘌呤是通路中间物，会被黄嘌呤氧化酶迅速推向尿酸，不会蓄积去抑制呼吸链。
quiz.explain_en: Purine nitrogen ends up locked in the urate ring and excreted, and since humans lack urate oxidase metabolism stops at uric acid, whose low solubility lets monosodium urate crystallise and cause gout — the very logic he uses later with the seafood broth. His ammonia toxicity claim is wrong: purine degradation does not end in free ammonia, which is the pyrimidine branch. What crystallises in joints is monosodium urate, not adenine; and hypoxanthine is an intermediate pushed on to urate by xanthine oxidase rather than accumulating to inhibit respiration.

quiz.q_zh: 关于腺嘌呤脱氨生成次黄嘌呤这一步，正确的说法是？
quiz.q_en: Which statement about the deamination of adenine to hypoxanthine is correct?

options.zh: 属于水解脱氨，释放游离氨，实际不可逆
options.en: It is hydrolytic deamination, releasing free ammonia, and irreversible

options.zh: 属于氧化脱氨，由氧分子直接接受氢原子
options.en: It is oxidative deamination with molecular oxygen accepting hydrogen

options.zh: 属于可逆平衡，加回一分子氨即得腺嘌呤
options.en: It is a reversible equilibrium; adding ammonia back regenerates adenine

options.zh: 属于转氨反应，把氨基交给 α-酮戊二酸
options.en: It is a transamination handing the amino group to α-ketoglutarate

quiz.explain_zh: 6 位氨基被水解掉、以游离 NH3 的形式离开，剩下 6-羰基就是次黄嘌呤，这个反应在生理条件下不往回走。老师说的可逆是错的，把氨加回去做不回腺嘌呤；恢复腺嘌呤骨架要走腺苷酸代琥珀酸合成酶那条路，氨基来自天冬氨酸。它也不是转氨反应，转氨不放游离氨、需要 PLP 和 α-酮酸受体；也不是用 O2 的氧化脱氨，那是氨基酸氧化酶的方式。
quiz.explain_en: The 6-amino group is hydrolysed off and leaves as free NH3, and the resulting 6-oxo compound is hypoxanthine; under physiological conditions the reaction does not run backwards. His claim of reversibility is wrong — adding ammonia back does not regenerate adenine; restoring the adenine framework requires the adenylosuccinate synthetase route with the nitrogen from aspartate. Nor is it transamination, which frees no ammonia and needs PLP with a keto acid acceptor, and nor is it O2-dependent oxidative deamination, the amino acid oxidase mode.

title_zh: 氨基与羰基的互换、黄嘌呤氧化酶两步氧化、尿酸与痛风
title_en: Amino to carbonyl, the two oxidations by xanthine oxidase, urate and gout

points.zh: 他给出一条通则：所有碱基代谢里，氨基被脱掉以后就变成羰基；反过来羰基也可以接受一分子氨基变回去，他说这两个基团可以随意互换。
points.en: He gave a general rule: throughout base metabolism, once an amino group is removed it becomes a carbonyl, and conversely a carbonyl can take up an amino group again — he called the two freely interchangeable.

points.zh: 腺嘌呤的第一步就是这个氨基变羰基，产物就是次黄嘌呤。
points.en: The first step for adenine is exactly this amino-to-carbonyl change, giving hypoxanthine.

points.zh: 鸟嘌呤那个位置本来就已经是羰基，不能再变，所以它只能把另一处的氨基脱掉。
points.en: In guanine that position is already a carbonyl and cannot change further, so it must lose the amino group at the other position.

points.zh: 脱掉之后那里也变成羰基，于是鸟嘌呤的产物在上下两个位置都是羰基，这个叫黄嘌呤。
points.en: Once removed, that position also becomes a carbonyl, so the guanine product bears carbonyls at both positions: xanthine.

points.zh: 次黄嘌呤和黄嘌呤长得很像，只差一个位置上的羰基，所以次黄嘌呤还可以再转化成黄嘌呤 —— 两条路最终汇到一起。
points.en: Hypoxanthine and xanthine look much alike, differing by one carbonyl, so hypoxanthine can be converted onward to xanthine; the two routes converge.

points.zh: 这里必须记住的酶是黄嘌呤氧化酶 xanthine oxidase，他强调这个酶比较重要。
points.en: The enzyme to remember here is xanthine oxidase, which he stressed as important.

points.zh: 关键点：次黄嘌呤氧化成黄嘌呤、黄嘌呤再氧化成尿酸，这两步其实是同一个酶催化的。
points.en: The key point: oxidation of hypoxanthine to xanthine and of xanthine to uric acid are catalysed by the same enzyme.

points.zh: 他接着说一分子尿酸「应该是」可以分解为三分子尿素，同时也说尿酸可以就以尿酸的形式直接排出体外。
points.en: He then said one uric acid 'should be able to' break down into three ureas, while also noting urate can simply be excreted as such.

points.zh: 尿酸的溶解度不高（上一章讲过），嘌呤摄入太多、尿酸来不及随尿排出就会痛风；海鲜汤、嘌呤汤嘌呤含量高，所以说少喝。
points.en: Uric acid is poorly soluble (covered in the previous chapter), so excess purine intake and urate that cannot leave in the urine fast enough cause gout; seafood and purine-rich broths are high in purines, hence the advice to go easy on them.

extra.zh: 「一分子尿酸可以分解为三分子尿素」不成立，他自己也用「应该是」打了折扣。人和其他灵长类没有尿酸氧化酶 urate oxidase（尿酸酶），尿酸就是嘌呤代谢的终产物，原样随尿排出，体内根本不把尿酸再降解成尿素。在保留尿酸酶的动物里，路径是尿酸 → 尿囊素 allantoin → 尿囊酸 → 2 分子尿素 + 乙醛酸，是 2 不是 3，而且这条路人身上没有。
extra.en: 'One uric acid breaks down into three ureas' does not hold, and he hedged it himself with 'should be'. Humans and other primates lack urate oxidase (uricase), so uric acid is the end product of purine metabolism and is excreted unchanged; the body does not degrade it to urea at all. In animals that kept uricase the route is urate → allantoin → allantoic acid → 2 urea + glyoxylate — two, not three — and we do not have it.

extra.zh: 人为什么这么容易痛风，答案就是这个缺失的酶。分解代谢在尿酸这一步就停了，而尿酸的溶解度又低；再加上肾脏排泄尿酸的能力有限（肾小球滤过的尿酸绝大部分被近端小管重吸收，净排泄量只是一小部分），限速在排泄端而不是分解端。老师说的「摄入嘌呤太多」只是负荷端的一个因素，临床上更多的高尿酸血症其实是排泄不足型。
extra.en: Why humans are so prone to gout comes down to that missing enzyme. Catabolism halts at uric acid, which is poorly soluble, and renal handling is limited — most filtered urate is reabsorbed in the proximal tubule and only a fraction is netted out — so the bottleneck is excretion rather than breakdown. High purine intake, his explanation, is only the load side; clinically, under-excretion is the more common cause of hyperuricaemia.

extra.zh: 黄嘌呤氧化酶值得多知道两句：它是含钼蝶呤和铁硫簇的酶，两步氧化中插入的氧原子来自水而不是 O2，同时把 O2 还原成 H2O2 和超氧，因此它也是缺血再灌注损伤里的一个自由基来源。别嘌呤醇 allopurinol 是次黄嘌呤的异构体，被这个酶自己氧化成氧嘌呤醇 oxypurinol 后紧紧结合还原态的钼中心，属于机制依赖性（自杀性）抑制，是降尿酸的经典药物 —— 它是人工合成的药，不是霉菌毒素。
extra.en: Xanthine oxidase is worth two more sentences: it is a molybdopterin and iron-sulfur enzyme whose inserted oxygen in both oxidations comes from water, not O2, while O2 is reduced to hydrogen peroxide and superoxide, making it a radical source in ischaemia-reperfusion injury. Allopurinol, an isomer of hypoxanthine, is oxidised by the enzyme itself to oxypurinol, which binds the reduced molybdenum centre tightly — mechanism-based (suicide) inhibition — and is the classic urate-lowering drug. It is a synthetic medicine, not a mould toxin.

extra.zh: 「氨基和羰基可以随意互换」只是画结构时的记忆口诀，不要当成一个可以来回跑的平衡。降解方向上是水解脱氨，放出游离 NH3，不可逆；把氨基装回环上走的是完全不同的合成或补救反应，例如 IMP + 天冬氨酸 + GTP → 腺苷酸代琥珀酸 → AMP，氮来自天冬氨酸而不是环境里的氨。两个方向的酶、辅因子和能量投入都不一样。
extra.en: 'Amino and carbonyl interconvert freely' is a drawing mnemonic, not a two-way equilibrium. The degradative direction is hydrolytic deamination releasing free NH3, and it is irreversible; putting an amino group back on the ring uses entirely different synthetic or salvage reactions, such as IMP + aspartate + GTP → adenylosuccinate → AMP, where the nitrogen comes from aspartate rather than ambient ammonia. The enzymes, cofactors and energy costs differ in the two directions.

quiz.q_zh: 次黄嘌呤→黄嘌呤→尿酸这两步氧化由几种酶催化？
quiz.q_en: How many enzymes catalyse hypoxanthine to xanthine to uric acid?

options.zh: 两种，先由脱氨酶再由尿酸合成酶接力完成
options.en: Two: a deaminase first, then urate synthase in relay

options.zh: 三种，每一步各有一个专一的氧化酶负责
options.en: Three: each step has its own dedicated oxidase

options.zh: 一种，两步都由黄嘌呤氧化酶催化完成
options.en: One: xanthine oxidase catalyses both oxidations

options.zh: 两种，分别是次黄嘌呤氧化酶和黄嘌呤氧化酶
options.en: Two: hypoxanthine oxidase and then xanthine oxidase

quiz.explain_zh: 老师专门强调过「其实这两个是同一个酶」：黄嘌呤氧化酶先把次黄嘌呤 C2 位氧化成黄嘌呤，再把黄嘌呤 C8 位氧化成尿酸。这也是别嘌呤醇一个药就能同时挡住两步、有效降尿酸的原因。不存在「次黄嘌呤氧化酶」这个独立的酶名，也没有所谓尿酸合成酶；三种专一氧化酶的说法更是把一个酶拆成了三个。
quiz.explain_en: He made a point of saying these are one and the same enzyme: xanthine oxidase oxidises hypoxanthine at C2 to xanthine, then xanthine at C8 to uric acid. That is also why one drug, allopurinol, blocks both steps and lowers urate effectively. There is no separate enzyme called hypoxanthine oxidase and no urate synthase, and postulating three dedicated oxidases splits one enzyme into three.

quiz.q_zh: 人体内嘌呤分解代谢的终产物是什么，为什么停在这里？
quiz.q_en: What is the end product of human purine catabolism, and why stop there?

options.zh: 尿酸，因为人缺少尿酸氧化酶无法再降解
options.en: Uric acid, because humans lack urate oxidase to degrade it further

options.zh: 尿囊素，因为人的尿囊酸酶活性极低而停住
options.en: Allantoin, because human allantoicase activity is far too low

options.zh: 尿素，因为一分子尿酸开环生成三分子尿素
options.en: Urea, because one urate ring opens into three molecules of urea

options.zh: 黄嘌呤，因为黄嘌呤氧化酶只能催化第一步
options.en: Xanthine, because xanthine oxidase catalyses only the first step

quiz.explain_zh: 人和其他灵长类的尿酸酶基因已经失活，尿酸没有下一站，只能原样从尿排出，这正是高尿酸血症和痛风的分子基础。尿囊素是有尿酸酶的动物的下一站，人根本走不到；尿酸变尿素是老师这里的口误，而且即便在有尿酸酶的动物里也是 2 分子而不是 3 分子；黄嘌呤氧化酶恰恰催化两步，把黄嘌呤一直推到尿酸。
quiz.explain_en: In humans and other primates the uricase gene is inactivated, so uric acid has no next stop and is excreted unchanged — the molecular basis of hyperuricaemia and gout. Allantoin is the next stop only in animals that retain uricase, which we never reach; urate to urea is the teacher's slip here, and even in uricase-bearing animals the yield is two molecules, not three; and xanthine oxidase in fact catalyses both steps, driving xanthine all the way to urate.

quiz.q_zh: 按老师讲的结构逻辑，黄嘌呤与次黄嘌呤的区别在哪里？
quiz.q_en: By his structural logic, how does xanthine differ from hypoxanthine?

options.zh: 黄嘌呤是五元环，次黄嘌呤多稠合了一个六元环
options.en: Xanthine is a five-membered ring, hypoxanthine has a fused six-ring

options.zh: 黄嘌呤上下两处都是羰基，次黄嘌呤只有一处
options.en: Xanthine bears carbonyls at both positions, hypoxanthine at one

options.zh: 黄嘌呤带核糖属于核苷，次黄嘌呤是游离的碱基
options.en: Xanthine carries ribose as a nucleoside, hypoxanthine is a free base

options.zh: 黄嘌呤保留一个氨基，次黄嘌呤已经全部脱氨
options.en: Xanthine keeps one amino group, hypoxanthine has lost them all

quiz.explain_zh: 腺嘌呤脱氨只得到一个羰基（次黄嘌呤），鸟嘌呤原本就有一个羰基、再脱一个氨基就得到两个羰基（黄嘌呤），所以次黄嘌呤被黄嘌呤氧化酶补上第二个含氧基团后就汇入黄嘌呤。两者都是已经脱完氨的产物，不存在黄嘌呤还留着氨基；两者都是嘌呤，都是六元环稠合五元环的双环；两者在这里讨论的都是游离碱基，与带不带核糖无关。
quiz.explain_en: Deaminating adenine yields one carbonyl (hypoxanthine); guanine already has one and loses an amino group to gain a second (xanthine), so once xanthine oxidase adds the second oxygen function to hypoxanthine the two routes merge. Both products are already fully deaminated, so xanthine retaining an amino group is wrong; both are purines, that is a six-membered ring fused to a five-membered one; and both are discussed here as free bases, independent of whether ribose is attached.

title_zh: 三个水平上的嘌呤代谢：核苷酸、核苷、碱基
title_en: Purine metabolism at three levels: nucleotide, nucleoside and base

points.zh: 他先把前面的内容定位：刚才那一整套降解是在碱基（base）的水平上讲的。
points.en: He first situated what came before: that whole degradation was described at the level of the base.

points.zh: 但这个过程不一定非要在碱基水平发生 —— 他脱口说「可以在蛋白质的水平上」，同一句立刻改口「不是蛋白」，正确的是核苷酸和核苷的水平。
points.en: But it need not happen at the base level — he blurted 'at the protein level', corrected himself within the same sentence to 'not protein', and settled on the nucleotide and nucleoside levels.

points.zh: 复习定义：核苷是没有磷酸的，核苷酸是有磷酸的；base 就只是右边那一小坨碱基。
points.en: A refresher on definitions: a nucleoside has no phosphate, a nucleotide does, and the base is just that small piece on the right.

points.zh: 他给的记忆法：只要带「核」这个字，代表的就是含核糖，所以核苷和核苷酸都含戊糖，碱基不含。
points.en: His mnemonic: any name containing the character for nucleo- implies ribose, so both nucleoside and nucleotide contain the pentose while the base does not.

points.zh: 结论：两种嘌呤都可以在三个水平上代谢 —— 核苷酸（他写 NT）、核苷、碱基。
points.en: The conclusion: both purines can be metabolised at three levels — nucleotide (he writes NT), nucleoside and base.

points.zh: 在核苷酸水平上：腺嘌呤核苷酸可以变成次黄嘌呤核苷酸，也就是右边的碱基换成次黄嘌呤，后面还接着核糖和磷酸。
points.en: At the nucleotide level, adenine nucleotide becomes hypoxanthine nucleotide — the base on the right is swapped for hypoxanthine while ribose and phosphate stay attached.

points.zh: 次黄嘌呤核苷酸再在酶的作用下把 phosphate 去掉，就生成次黄嘌呤核苷；在核苷水平上也能发生同样的转化，用的基本是差不多的酶。
points.en: Hypoxanthine nucleotide then loses its phosphate enzymatically to give hypoxanthine nucleoside, and the same conversion also happens at the nucleoside level with much the same enzymes.

points.zh: 最终次黄嘌呤核苷把核糖也去掉，变成次黄嘌呤，再被氧化成黄嘌呤 —— 他这里说黄嘌呤「就变成这个尿素了」。
points.en: Finally hypoxanthine nucleoside loses the ribose to give hypoxanthine, which is oxidised to xanthine — and here he said xanthine 'becomes urea'.

points.zh: 他把脱磷酸那个酶叫核苷酸酶，并总结成「条条大路通罗马」：腺嘌呤核苷酸和次黄嘌呤核苷酸都可以减一分子磷酸变成对应的核苷，最后都汇到同一个终点。
points.en: He named the dephosphorylating enzyme a nucleotidase and summed up with 'all roads lead to Rome': both adenine and hypoxanthine nucleotides can shed a phosphate to the corresponding nucleoside, and all routes end at the same point.

extra.zh: 「黄嘌呤就变成这个尿素了」应为尿酸 uric acid。整条路是次黄嘌呤 →（黄嘌呤氧化酶）→ 黄嘌呤 →（同一个酶）→ 尿酸。他在约 00:59:01 和 00:59:34 讲的都是尿酸，说明这是重复出现的口误而不是概念错误，但本段内没有改口，笔记要按尿酸记。
extra.en: 'Xanthine becomes urea' should be uric acid. The route is hypoxanthine → (xanthine oxidase) → xanthine → (same enzyme) → uric acid. He said uric acid correctly around 00:59:01 and 00:59:34, so this is a recurring slip rather than a conceptual error, but he does not take it back within this stretch; write urate in your notes.

extra.zh: 他在结尾自己问「这可能是什么酶」，答案课上没给，但这张「条条大路通罗马」的图每一步都有名字：AMP →（AMP 脱氨酶）→ IMP；AMP →（5'-核苷酸酶）→ 腺苷；腺苷 →（腺苷脱氨酶 ADA）→ 肌苷；IMP →（5'-核苷酸酶）→ 肌苷；肌苷 →（嘌呤核苷磷酸化酶 PNP，磷酸解）→ 次黄嘌呤 + 核糖-1-磷酸；再由黄嘌呤氧化酶两步推到尿酸。他说的「脱磷酸的核苷酸酶」就是 5'-核苷酸酶。
extra.en: He asks at the end what enzyme this might be and never answers, but every step of that 'all roads lead to Rome' diagram has a name: AMP → (AMP deaminase) → IMP; AMP → (5'-nucleotidase) → adenosine; adenosine → (adenosine deaminase, ADA) → inosine; IMP → (5'-nucleotidase) → inosine; inosine → (purine nucleoside phosphorylase, PNP, phosphorolysis) → hypoxanthine + ribose-1-phosphate; then xanthine oxidase in two steps to urate. The dephosphorylating nucleotidase he mentions is 5'-nucleotidase.

extra.zh: 中文按结构命名、英文用俗名，同一个分子两套名字，考试两种都可能出现：次黄嘌呤核苷酸 = IMP = 肌苷酸；次黄嘌呤核苷 = 肌苷 inosine；腺嘌呤核苷 = 腺苷 adenosine；腺嘌呤核苷酸 = AMP = 腺苷酸；鸟嘌呤核苷 = 鸟苷 guanosine。老师说的「次黄嘌呤核苷酸」绕口，换成 IMP 一下就清楚了，而且 IMP 正是嘌呤从头合成的分叉点，后面还会再见到它。
extra.en: Chinese names these compounds structurally while English uses trivial names, so each molecule has two labels and either may appear on an exam: hypoxanthine nucleotide = IMP = inosinate; hypoxanthine nucleoside = inosine; adenine nucleoside = adenosine; adenine nucleotide = AMP; guanine nucleoside = guanosine. His mouthful 'hypoxanthine nucleotide' becomes clear the moment you call it IMP, and IMP is also the branch point of de novo purine synthesis, which returns later.

extra.zh: 这条降解支路不是废物处理管道，两个酶的缺陷各对应一种免疫缺陷病：ADA 缺陷时腺苷和脱氧腺苷蓄积、dATP 抑制核糖核苷酸还原酶而毒害淋巴细胞，就是重症联合免疫缺陷 SCID；PNP 缺陷主要打击 T 细胞。反过来这也解释了为什么淋巴细胞对嘌呤代谢的干扰特别敏感，是免疫抑制药（如硫唑嘌呤经 6-巯基嘌呤）的作用基础。
extra.en: This catabolic branch is not a waste chute: deficiency of either enzyme gives an immunodeficiency. In ADA deficiency, adenosine and deoxyadenosine accumulate and dATP inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, poisoning lymphocytes — severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID); PNP deficiency mainly hits T cells. Conversely this explains why lymphocytes are unusually sensitive to interference with purine metabolism, the basis of immunosuppressants such as azathioprine acting through 6-mercaptopurine.

quiz.q_zh: 他反复念的「次黄嘌呤核苷酸」，用英文俗名叫什么？
quiz.q_en: What is the trivial English name of the hypoxanthine nucleotide he kept repeating?

options.zh: XMP 黄苷酸，即黄嘌呤核苷加一个磷酸
options.en: XMP or xanthylate, that is xanthosine plus a phosphate

options.zh: AMP 腺苷酸，即腺嘌呤核苷加一个磷酸
options.en: AMP or adenylate, that is adenosine plus one phosphate

options.zh: 肌苷 inosine，即次黄嘌呤加一个核糖
options.en: Inosine, that is hypoxanthine plus one ribose sugar

options.zh: IMP 肌苷酸，即次黄嘌呤核苷加一个磷酸
options.en: IMP or inosinate, that is inosine plus one phosphate

quiz.explain_zh: 次黄嘌呤 + 核糖 + 磷酸就是 IMP，中文也叫肌苷酸，它既是嘌呤降解路上的节点，也是从头合成的分叉点。肌苷是去掉磷酸后的核苷，比 IMP 少一个磷酸；XMP 的碱基是黄嘌呤而不是次黄嘌呤，是 GMP 合成的前一步；AMP 的碱基是腺嘌呤，是被 AMP 脱氨酶转成 IMP 的那个起点。
quiz.explain_en: Hypoxanthine plus ribose plus phosphate is IMP, also called inosinate, both a node on the purine degradation route and the branch point of de novo synthesis. Inosine is the nucleoside left after the phosphate is removed, one phosphate short of IMP; XMP carries xanthine rather than hypoxanthine and is the step before GMP; and AMP carries adenine and is the starting point that AMP deaminase converts to IMP.

quiz.q_zh: 他说的「减一分子磷酸变成对应的核苷」由哪类酶完成？
quiz.q_en: Which class of enzyme carries out his 'lose one phosphate to give the nucleoside'?

options.zh: 核苷酸酶，水解核糖 5' 位的磷酸酯键
options.en: Nucleotidase, hydrolysing the phosphoester bond at the ribose 5'

options.zh: 核苷磷酸化酶，用无机磷酸解开糖苷键
options.en: Nucleoside phosphorylase, opening the glycoside with phosphate

options.zh: 腺苷脱氨酶，把腺苷上的氨基水解脱去
options.en: Adenosine deaminase, hydrolysing the amino group off adenosine

options.zh: 磷酸二酯酶，切开骨架上的磷酸二酯键
options.en: Phosphodiesterase, cutting the phosphodiester bonds of the backbone

quiz.explain_zh: 核苷酸 → 核苷这一步是脱磷酸，由 5'-核苷酸酶水解核糖 5' 位的磷酸单酯键完成，老师最后也用了「核苷酸酶」这个名字。核苷磷酸化酶动的是下一步的 N-糖苷键，产物是碱基加核糖-1-磷酸；腺苷脱氨酶改的是碱基上的氨基，磷酸早已不在；磷酸二酯酶作用在长链骨架上，那是更早的消化步骤。
quiz.explain_en: Nucleotide to nucleoside is a dephosphorylation, done by 5'-nucleotidase hydrolysing the phosphomonoester at ribose 5', and he uses the name nucleotidase himself at the end. Nucleoside phosphorylase attacks the N-glycosidic bond one step later, giving base plus ribose-1-phosphate; adenosine deaminase alters the amino group on the base, by which point the phosphate is long gone; and phosphodiesterase acts on the polymer backbone, an earlier digestive step.

title_zh: 嘌呤分解的汇聚：从核苷酸到尿酸，以及黄嘌呤氧化酶的钼
title_en: Purine catabolism converges: nucleotide to urate, and the molybdenum of xanthine oxidase

points.zh: 他用「条条大路通罗马」概括嘌呤分解：从上往下走是脱磷酸，从左往右走是脱氨基，两个方向最后都汇到同一个中间物。
points.en: He sums up purine catabolism as all roads leading to Rome: moving down the chart means losing phosphate, moving right means losing the amino group, and both directions converge on one intermediate.

points.zh: 脱磷酸这一步他标的酶是核苷酸酶：腺嘌呤核苷酸减一分子磷酸变腺嘌呤核苷，次黄嘌呤核苷酸减一分子磷酸变次黄嘌呤核苷。
points.en: The dephosphorylation step he labels as a nucleotidase: adenine nucleotide minus one phosphate gives adenosine, hypoxanthine nucleotide minus one phosphate gives inosine.

points.zh: 汇聚点是次黄嘌呤核苷（肌苷 inosine），无论从哪条路进来都到这里。
points.en: The convergence point is inosine, the hypoxanthine nucleoside, whichever route the molecule came in by.

points.zh: 下一步是把核糖去掉——他在板上用一个五元环表示核糖——剩下游离的碱基次黄嘌呤。
points.en: The next step removes the ribose, which he draws as a five-membered ring on the board, leaving the free base hypoxanthine.

points.zh: 次黄嘌呤再被氧化成黄嘌呤，黄嘌呤再被氧化一次；此处他说黄嘌呤「变成尿素」。
points.en: Hypoxanthine is then oxidised to xanthine, and xanthine oxidised once more; at this point he says xanthine becomes urea.

points.zh: 他特别提黄嘌呤氧化酶很重要，因为人体之所以需要钼元素，就是这个酶要用。
points.en: He flags xanthine oxidase as important because the reason the human body needs molybdenum at all is this enzyme.

points.zh: 他在板上写下「钼」字，强调黄嘌呤氧化酶上带着钼元素，通常的氧化过程需要钼参与。
points.en: He writes the character for molybdenum on the board, stressing that xanthine oxidase carries molybdenum and that its usual oxidation needs the metal.

points.zh: 他把钼的作用类比成镁离子或锰离子的原理，说「有点像」。
points.en: He likens the role of molybdenum to that of magnesium or manganese ions, saying the principle is somewhat similar.

points.zh: 结尾引出别嘌呤醇（他也叫别黄嘌呤）：它跟次黄嘌呤的区别是一个氮原子的位置换了一下。
points.en: He closes by introducing allopurinol, noting that compared with hypoxanthine one nitrogen atom sits in a different position.

extra.zh: 黄嘌呤氧化后的产物是尿酸 uric acid，不是尿素 urea。这句口误在本段出现两次（01:02:47 一次、01:04:25 一次）。他随后在 01:07:06 明确要求写下「嘌呤的最终产物是尿酸」，算是间接改回来了，但没有点名收回前面那两句。
extra.en: The product of xanthine oxidation is uric acid, not urea. He slips twice in this stretch (once around 01:02:47 and again at 01:04:25). At 01:07:06 he dictates the sentence that the end product of purine metabolism is uric acid, which corrects it indirectly, though he never names the earlier slip.

extra.zh: 黄嘌呤氧化酶（XO）是一个酶催化连续两步（次黄嘌呤→黄嘌呤→尿酸），辅因子有钼-蝶呤 molybdopterin、FAD 和两组 [2Fe-2S]。反应中钼在 Mo(VI) 与 Mo(IV) 之间循环，掺进底物的那个氧原子来自水而不是 O2；电子经 Fe-S 传给 FAD，再交给 O2，产超氧和 H2O2——这是缺血再灌注损伤里 XO 被反复提到的原因。
extra.en: Xanthine oxidase (XO) runs both oxidations with one active site (hypoxanthine to xanthine to urate). Its cofactors are a molybdopterin centre, FAD and two [2Fe-2S] clusters. Molybdenum cycles between Mo(VI) and Mo(IV), and the oxygen inserted into the substrate comes from water, not from O2; electrons pass through the Fe-S clusters to FAD and on to O2, generating superoxide and H2O2 — which is why XO keeps appearing in ischaemia-reperfusion injury.

extra.zh: 钼跟 Mg2+、Mn2+ 的类比只在「都是酶需要的金属」这一层成立。Mg2+/Mn2+ 通常只是配位底物、中和磷酸负电荷的结构性离子，本身价态不变；钼在这里是直接参与氧原子转移的氧化还原中心，价态每一轮都变。把两者等同会让人以为别嘌呤醇的作用是把一个「辅助离子」抢走。
extra.en: The comparison with Mg2+ and Mn2+ holds only at the level of both being metals an enzyme needs. Mg2+ and Mn2+ are usually structural ions that coordinate substrate and neutralise phosphate charge without changing oxidation state; the molybdenum here is a redox centre that changes valence every turnover and performs the oxygen transfer itself. Treating them as equivalent invites the idea that allopurinol simply removes a helper ion.

extra.zh: 人体内的脱氨基主要不在游离碱基层次，而在核苷/核苷酸层次：腺苷脱氨酶 ADA 把腺苷变肌苷，AMP 脱氨酶把 AMP 变 IMP。ADA 缺陷即重症联合免疫缺陷 SCID，是这一步唯一的经典临床落点。游离腺嘌呤脱氨酶主要见于微生物。
extra.en: In humans deamination happens mainly at the nucleoside/nucleotide level rather than on the free base: adenosine deaminase (ADA) converts adenosine to inosine and AMP deaminase converts AMP to IMP. ADA deficiency is severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID), the classic clinical landing point for this step. Deaminases acting on free adenine are largely microbial.

quiz.q_zh: 次黄嘌呤经黄嘌呤氧化酶连续两步氧化，在人体内的终产物是什么？
quiz.q_en: Hypoxanthine is oxidised twice in a row by xanthine oxidase. What is the end product in humans?

options.zh: 尿酸，人没有尿酸酶所以到此为止
options.en: Uric acid — humans have no uricase to go further

options.zh: 尿素，由尿酸经尿素循环转化而来
options.en: Urea, formed from uric acid in the urea cycle

options.zh: 尿囊素，人体尿酸酶氧化尿酸的产物
options.en: Allantoin, the product of human uricase enzyme

options.zh: 乙醛酸，尿囊酸被裂解之后释放出来
options.en: Glyoxylate, split off from allantoate by lyase

quiz.explain_zh: 尿酸是人和其他灵长类嘌呤代谢的终点，因为编码尿酸酶的基因已经假基因化。尿囊素只在保留尿酸酶的物种里出现，乙醛酸更在尿囊酸裂解之后才释放，两者在人体内都没有。尿素来自尿素循环，与嘌呤环的碳氮无关——老师此处口误说成尿素，01:07:06 他自己写下的结论句才是对的。
quiz.explain_en: Uric acid is where purine catabolism stops in humans and other primates, because the uricase gene is a pseudogene. Allantoin only appears in species that kept uricase, and glyoxylate is released even further downstream from allantoate; neither exists in humans. Urea comes from the urea cycle and has nothing to do with the purine ring — the teacher's slip here, corrected by the sentence he dictates at 01:07:06.

quiz.q_zh: 黄嘌呤氧化酶里的钼是以什么方式参与催化的？
quiz.q_en: How does the molybdenum in xanthine oxidase take part in catalysis?

options.zh: 作为电子受体，把电子直接交给 NAD+ 分子
options.en: An electron acceptor handing electrons to NAD+

options.zh: 作为氧化还原中心，钼在 VI 与 IV 价间循环
options.en: A redox centre cycling between Mo(VI) and Mo(IV)

options.zh: 作为底物结合位点，与嘌呤环的 N7 形成配位键
options.en: A binding site coordinating the purine ring N7

options.zh: 作为结构离子，像 Mg2+ 那样中和磷酸负电荷
options.en: A structural ion neutralising charge, like Mg2+

quiz.explain_zh: 钼-蝶呤中心每一轮都在 Mo(VI) 和 Mo(IV) 之间往返，掺进底物的氧来自水。它不是 Mg2+ 那种价态不变的结构离子；电子也不交给 NAD+，而是经 [2Fe-2S] 传到 FAD 再给 O2；底物的结合由活性口袋的氨基酸完成，不靠钼与 N7 配位。这一点正是别嘌呤醇作用机制的前提。
quiz.explain_en: The molybdopterin centre shuttles between Mo(VI) and Mo(IV) each turnover, and the oxygen inserted into substrate comes from water. It is not a fixed-valence structural ion like Mg2+; the electrons do not go to NAD+ but travel through the [2Fe-2S] clusters to FAD and then O2; and substrate is held by active-site residues, not by a metal bond to N7. This is exactly the premise for how allopurinol works.

title_zh: 别嘌呤醇的说法、「嘌呤终产物是尿酸」，转入嘧啶分解
title_en: What he says about allopurinol, the urate take-home line, and the switch to pyrimidines

points.zh: 他说别嘌呤醇会和黄嘌呤氧化酶上的钼离子发生螯合，「有点像 EDTA 的作用把金属离子给螯合了」，直接导致酶失活。
points.en: He says allopurinol chelates the molybdenum ion on xanthine oxidase, comparing it to EDTA pulling a metal ion away, and that this inactivates the enzyme outright.

points.zh: 他说这个东西存在于黄曲霉菌、黄曲霉素之类微生物的次生代谢产物里。
points.en: He places the compound among the secondary metabolites of microbes such as Aspergillus flavus and aflatoxin.

points.zh: 他说人吃进去以后在酶的催化下产生别黄嘌呤，「这个东西就会把这个酶给干死」，所以对人毒性蛮大。
points.en: He says that once eaten it is converted by the enzyme into alloxanthine, which kills the enzyme off, and concludes that it is quite toxic to humans.

points.zh: 他借这一段收束钼的话题：钼离子在人体内就是黄嘌呤氧化酶需要它。
points.en: He wraps up the molybdenum thread with the line that in the human body it is xanthine oxidase that needs the metal.

points.zh: 画一条线收尾，要求写下一句话：嘌呤的代谢最终产物是尿酸，并强调「任何情况下」都记这句。
points.en: He draws a line to close the section and dictates one sentence to write down: the end product of purine metabolism is uric acid, to be remembered under all circumstances.

points.zh: 转入嘧啶代谢，强调嘧啶跟嘌呤「完全是两条路子」，嘧啶是单环、一共三种。
points.en: He moves to pyrimidine metabolism, stressing that it is a completely separate route from purines, that pyrimidines are single-ring and that there are three of them.

points.zh: 从 C 开始：第一步由胞嘧啶脱氨酶脱掉氨基，他说凡是带氨基的碱基代谢第一步都是脱氨。
points.en: He starts with C: the first step is removal of the amino group by cytosine deaminase, and he generalises that any amino-bearing base begins its catabolism by deamination.

points.zh: 他给的理由是氨基对人体有害，脱下来的氨基经尿素循环排出去；C 脱氨以后变成 U。
points.en: His reason is that the amino group is harmful and the nitrogen leaves through the urea cycle; C after deamination becomes U.

points.zh: U 已经没办法再脱氨，所以机体改为给环上的双键加两个氢，变成二氢尿嘧啶；他说催化的这个脱氢酶不重要、不用记。
points.en: U can no longer be deaminated, so the body instead adds two hydrogens across the ring double bond to give dihydrouracil; he says the dehydrogenase involved is not important enough to memorise.

extra.zh: 这是本段最要紧的一条。别嘌呤醇 allopurinol 是人工合成的抗痛风药，不是黄曲霉的次生代谢产物，对人也不是毒物——它正是临床上用来降尿酸的一线药。结构上它是次黄嘌呤的异构体（吡唑并嘧啶，氮的位置换了，这一点他描述对了）。机制上它被黄嘌呤氧化酶自己氧化成氧嘌呤醇 oxypurinol（他叫别黄嘌呤），氧嘌呤醇与酶的还原态 Mo(IV) 中心结合得极紧、解离极慢，属于机制依赖性（自杀性）抑制，不是 EDTA 式把金属离子从酶上螯合走。他在 01:06:32 把顺序讲回来了（吃进去的是别嘌呤醇，被酶催化后才是别黄嘌呤），那半句是对的。
extra.en: The most important correction in this stretch. Allopurinol is a synthetic anti-gout drug, not an Aspergillus metabolite, and it is not a poison — it is the first-line urate-lowering agent. Structurally it is an isomer of hypoxanthine (a pyrazolopyrimidine with the nitrogen moved, which he describes correctly). Mechanistically xanthine oxidase itself oxidises it to oxypurinol, which binds the reduced Mo(IV) centre extremely tightly and dissociates very slowly — mechanism-based, suicide inhibition, not EDTA-style chelation of the metal away from the enzyme. At 01:06:32 he gets the order right (allopurinol goes in, the enzyme makes alloxanthine), and that half is correct.

extra.zh: 黄曲霉毒素 aflatoxin B1 才是黄曲霉的次生代谢产物，它是已知最强的天然肝致癌物之一，经 CYP450 活化成环氧化物再加合到 DNA 鸟嘌呤 N7 上。它和别嘌呤醇没有任何关系。别嘌呤醇真正的不良反应是超敏综合征（与 HLA-B*58:01 相关），不是「霉菌毒性」。
extra.en: Aflatoxin B1 is the Aspergillus flavus secondary metabolite — one of the most potent natural liver carcinogens, activated by CYP450 to an epoxide that adducts guanine N7 in DNA. It has nothing to do with allopurinol. Allopurinol's real serious adverse effect is a hypersensitivity syndrome linked to HLA-B*58:01, not any kind of mould toxicity.

extra.zh: 「嘌呤终产物是尿酸」只对人和其他灵长类成立，原因是尿酸酶 uricase 基因在进化中假基因化了。保留尿酸酶的物种终点是尿囊素 allantoin，再往下是尿囊酸→2 分子尿素 + 乙醛酸。重组尿酸酶（拉布立酶 rasburicase）就是靠把尿酸变成可溶的尿囊素来处理肿瘤溶解综合征的。
extra.en: The line that purines end at uric acid holds only for humans and other primates, because the uricase gene was pseudogenised. Species that kept uricase end at allantoin, then allantoate, then two ureas plus glyoxylate. Recombinant uricase (rasburicase) works precisely by converting urate to soluble allantoin, which is how tumour lysis syndrome is managed.

extra.zh: 哺乳动物基本没有作用于游离胞嘧啶的脱氨酶——C 的脱氨主要在核苷/核苷酸水平（胞苷脱氨酶 CDA、dCMP 脱氨酶）。作用于游离胞嘧啶的 cytosine deaminase 是细菌和真菌的酶，正因为人没有它，才被拿来做自杀基因治疗（把 5-氟胞嘧啶转成 5-FU）。另外有毒的是脱下来的游离氨 NH3/NH4+，氨基还连在分子上的时候并不是毒物。
extra.en: Mammals essentially lack a deaminase acting on free cytosine — C is deaminated at the nucleoside/nucleotide level by cytidine deaminase (CDA) and dCMP deaminase. Cytosine deaminase acting on the free base is a bacterial and fungal enzyme, and it is precisely because humans lack it that it is used in suicide gene therapy (converting 5-fluorocytosine to 5-FU). Also, what is toxic is the free ammonia released, not an amino group still attached to a molecule.

quiz.q_zh: 别嘌呤醇究竟是什么？
quiz.q_en: What is allopurinol actually?

options.zh: 黄曲霉的次生代谢产物，对人有较强毒性
options.en: A secondary metabolite of Aspergillus, toxic to us

options.zh: 从牛肉等高嘌呤食物中提取的天然碱基
options.en: A natural base extracted from purine-rich beef

options.zh: 由肝脏合成的一种内源性黄嘌呤氧化酶抑制剂
options.en: An endogenous xanthine oxidase inhibitor from liver

options.zh: 人工合成的次黄嘌呤异构体，用于治疗痛风
options.en: A synthetic hypoxanthine isomer used against gout

quiz.explain_zh: 别嘌呤醇是 1960 年代合成的吡唑并嘧啶，是次黄嘌呤的异构体，临床上用于降尿酸治痛风。说它是黄曲霉的次生代谢产物、说它有较强毒性都不成立——那是黄曲霉毒素的性质；它也不是从食物里提取的碱基，更不是肝脏合成的内源性物质，人体不产生这种化合物。
quiz.explain_en: Allopurinol is a pyrazolopyrimidine synthesised in the 1960s, an isomer of hypoxanthine, used clinically to lower urate in gout. Calling it an Aspergillus metabolite or describing it as quite toxic both fail — those are properties of aflatoxin; it is not a base extracted from food, and it is not made endogenously by the liver, since the body produces no such compound.

quiz.q_zh: 别嘌呤醇抑制黄嘌呤氧化酶的机制是什么？
quiz.q_en: By what mechanism does allopurinol inhibit xanthine oxidase?

options.zh: 共价修饰活性中心的半胱氨酸巯基使其失活
options.en: Covalently modifies an active-site cysteine thiol

options.zh: 与酶竞争性结合 FAD 位点，阻断电子传递
options.en: Competes at the FAD site and blocks electron flow

options.zh: 被酶氧化成氧嘌呤醇，紧扣住还原态钼中心
options.en: The enzyme oxidises it to oxypurinol, which binds Mo

options.zh: 像 EDTA 一样把钼离子从酶蛋白上螯合下来
options.en: Chelates the molybdenum off the enzyme like EDTA

quiz.explain_zh: 别嘌呤醇本身是底物类似物，被黄嘌呤氧化酶氧化成氧嘌呤醇（老师说的别黄嘌呤），氧嘌呤醇随后与还原态 Mo(IV) 紧密结合、解离极慢，把酶锁死——这叫机制依赖性抑制。它不结合 FAD 位点；也不像 EDTA 那样把金属螯合出来，钼始终留在酶上；抑制也不靠共价修饰半胱氨酸。
quiz.explain_en: Allopurinol is a substrate analogue: xanthine oxidase oxidises it to oxypurinol, which then binds the reduced Mo(IV) centre very tightly and comes off very slowly, locking the enzyme up — mechanism-based inhibition. It does not act at the FAD site; it does not strip the metal out the way EDTA would, since the molybdenum stays on the enzyme; and inhibition does not involve covalent cysteine modification.

quiz.q_zh: 哺乳动物体内胞嘧啶的脱氨主要发生在哪个层次？
quiz.q_en: At which level does cytosine deamination mainly occur in mammals?

options.zh: 核苷与核苷酸层次，由胞苷脱氨酶等催化
options.en: On nucleosides and nucleotides, by cytidine deaminase

options.zh: DNA 层次，由碱基切除修复系统直接完成
options.en: On DNA itself, through the base excision repair path

options.zh: 游离碱基层次，由细菌型胞嘧啶脱氨酶催化
options.en: On the free base, by a bacterial cytosine deaminase

options.zh: 三磷酸层次，由 CTP 脱氨酶转成 UTP
options.en: At the triphosphate level, by a CTP deaminase

quiz.explain_zh: 哺乳动物用胞苷脱氨酶 CDA（胞苷→尿苷）和 dCMP 脱氨酶（dCMP→dUMP），都在核苷/核苷酸水平。作用于游离胞嘧啶的脱氨酶是细菌和真菌的酶，人没有；哺乳动物没有把 CTP 直接脱氨成 UTP 的途径；DNA 上的胞嘧啶自发脱氨确实存在，但那是损伤，由 UNG 走碱基切除修复清除，不是正常的分解代谢路线。
quiz.explain_en: Mammals use cytidine deaminase (cytidine to uridine) and dCMP deaminase (dCMP to dUMP), both at the nucleoside/nucleotide level. A deaminase acting on the free base is bacterial and fungal and absent in humans; mammals have no route deaminating CTP straight to UTP; and spontaneous deamination of cytosine in DNA does happen, but that is damage cleared by UNG-driven base excision repair, not a catabolic pathway.

title_zh: C 与 U 的终产物 β-丙氨酸，胸腺嘧啶的甲基与 SAM
title_en: β-alanine as the end of C and U, and thymine's methyl group with SAM

points.zh: 二氢尿嘧啶经进一步代谢，最终变成 β-丙氨酸（β-alanine）。
points.en: Dihydrouracil goes on through further steps to end as β-alanine.

points.zh: 他要求写下结论句：胞嘧啶和尿嘧啶的代谢最终产物是 β-丙氨酸，并说不写下来以后复习会很混乱。
points.en: He dictates the take-home sentence that cytosine and uracil both end at β-alanine, warning that without it the notes will be confusing later.

points.zh: 他说 β-丙氨酸的主要去向是掺入变成丙二酸单酰CoA。
points.en: He says β-alanine's main fate is to be incorporated into malonyl-CoA.

points.zh: 丙二酸单酰CoA 被他点名为脂肪酸合成的起始原料。
points.en: He names malonyl-CoA as the starting material for fatty acid synthesis.

points.zh: 转到 T：他说胸腺嘧啶在整个核苷酸代谢里都是「特立独行」的一个东西。
points.en: Turning to T, he calls thymine the maverick of the whole of nucleotide metabolism.

points.zh: 原因是这么多碱基里只有它在那个位置多了一个甲基。
points.en: The reason is that among all these bases only thymine carries an extra methyl group at that position.

points.zh: 他说这个甲基一般是 SAM 给的，并把 SAM 描述成「腺嘌呤加了一个甲硫氨酸」的那个东西，甲基来自甲硫氨酸。
points.en: He says the methyl usually comes from SAM, describing SAM as adenine plus methionine, with the methyl group supplied by the methionine.

points.zh: T 的分解第一步跟尿嘧啶一样：因为机体没办法直接把甲基处理掉，就先给双键加两个氢，把环变成饱和的还原形式。
points.en: Thymine's catabolism starts like uracil's: because the body cannot deal with the methyl directly, two hydrogens are added across the double bond to give a saturated, reduced ring.

points.zh: 接下来经一系列代谢，最终生成 β-氨基异丁酸。
points.en: A further series of steps then yields β-aminoisobutyrate.

extra.zh: SAM 是 S-腺苷甲硫氨酸 S-adenosylmethionine，不是「腺嘌呤 + 甲硫氨酸」。甲硫氨酸的硫连在腺苷（腺嘌呤 + 核糖）的 5′-碳上，少了核糖这一步整个结构说不通。关键在于这样形成的是三价锍离子（硫上带正电荷），正电荷让 S-甲基的转移势能很高，SAM 才成为通用甲基供体。
extra.en: SAM is S-adenosylmethionine, not adenine plus methionine. The sulfur of methionine is bonded to the 5'-carbon of adenosine (adenine plus ribose); leave the ribose out and the structure makes no sense. The point is that this creates a positively charged sulfonium centre, and that charge is what gives the S-methyl group its high transfer potential and makes SAM the universal methyl donor.

extra.zh: DNA 里 T 的甲基并不是 SAM 给的。dTMP 由胸苷酸合酶 thymidylate synthase 用 N5,N10-亚甲基四氢叶酸把 dUMP 甲基化而来，叶酸在这一步被氧化成二氢叶酸，需要 DHFR 再还原回去。SAM 供的是另一类甲基化，例如 DNA 上的 5-甲基胞嘧啶、组蛋白甲基化、肾上腺素合成。这也正是 5-氟尿嘧啶（抑制胸苷酸合酶）和甲氨蝶呤（抑制 DHFR）两个药的作用点。
extra.en: The methyl on T in DNA does not come from SAM. dTMP is made by thymidylate synthase, which methylates dUMP using N5,N10-methylene tetrahydrofolate; the folate is oxidised to dihydrofolate in the process and must be reduced back by DHFR. SAM supplies a different class of methylations — 5-methylcytosine in DNA, histone methylation, adrenaline synthesis. This is exactly where 5-fluorouracil (blocking thymidylate synthase) and methotrexate (blocking DHFR) act.

extra.zh: 他说「不用记」的那个酶是二氢嘧啶脱氢酶 DPD，嘧啶分解的限速步。名字叫脱氢酶，在分解方向上跑的却是还原反应——用 NADPH 把 U 加氢成二氢尿嘧啶，方向很容易记反。DPD 活性低的人用 5-氟尿嘧啶会出现严重甚至致命的毒性，临床上会先做 DPYD 基因型筛查。
extra.en: The enzyme he waves off is dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD), the rate-limiting step of pyrimidine catabolism. Despite the name it runs in the reductive direction here, using NADPH to add hydrogens to uracil — a direction students routinely reverse. People with low DPD activity suffer severe or fatal toxicity from 5-fluorouracil, which is why DPYD genotyping is done before treatment.

extra.zh: β-丙氨酸不只是一个代谢终点：它与组氨酸缩合成肌肽 carnosine，是骨骼肌里重要的 pH 缓冲物质。而 β-丙氨酸的碳要走到丙二酸单酰CoA，中间还要先转氨、经丙二酸半醛氧化，不是一步「掺入」。
extra.en: β-alanine is not merely an endpoint: condensed with histidine it forms carnosine, a significant pH buffer in skeletal muscle. And getting its carbons to malonyl-CoA requires transamination and oxidation through malonate semialdehyde first — it is not a single incorporation step.

quiz.q_zh: 尿嘧啶进入分解代谢的第一步化学变化是什么？
quiz.q_en: What is the first chemical change when uracil enters catabolism?

options.zh: 环上的双键加上两个氢，还原成二氢尿嘧啶
options.en: Two hydrogens are added across the ring double bond

options.zh: 直接开环水解，生成氨甲酰-β-丙氨酸
options.en: Direct ring opening to give carbamoyl-β-alanine

options.zh: 先磷酸化成 UMP，再由核苷酸酶去磷酸
options.en: Phosphorylation to UMP, then loss of the phosphate

options.zh: 脱去 4 位氨基，由胞嘧啶脱氨酶催化
options.en: Removal of the 4-amino group by cytosine deaminase

quiz.explain_zh: U 的 4 位已经是酮基，没有氨基可脱，所以机体改走还原：DPD 用 NADPH 把 5,6 位双键加氢生成二氢尿嘧啶。脱氨那一步属于 C，不属于 U。开环生成氨甲酰-β-丙氨酸确实发生，但是在还原之后由二氢嘧啶酶催化的第二步。先磷酸化再去磷酸是无意义的循环，分解方向上不存在。
quiz.explain_en: Position 4 of uracil is already a keto group, so there is no amino group to lose and the cell reduces instead: DPD uses NADPH to hydrogenate the 5,6 double bond, giving dihydrouracil. Deamination belongs to C, not U. Ring opening to carbamoyl-β-alanine does happen, but as the second step after reduction, catalysed by dihydropyrimidinase. Phosphorylating to UMP and then removing the phosphate would be a futile cycle and is not part of catabolism.

quiz.q_zh: SAM 的正确结构组成是什么？
quiz.q_en: What is the correct structural make-up of SAM?

options.zh: 腺苷的 5′-碳连在甲硫氨酸的硫上
options.en: Adenosine 5'-carbon bonded to the sulfur

options.zh: 腺嘌呤碱基与甲硫氨酸直接相连
options.en: Adenine base joined directly to methionine

options.zh: 腺苷二磷酸与甲硫氨酸缩合而成
options.en: ADP condensed with the methionine backbone

options.zh: 腺嘌呤核苷酸与半胱氨酸相连
options.en: An adenine nucleotide linked to cysteine

quiz.explain_zh: SAM = S-腺苷甲硫氨酸：ATP 与甲硫氨酸反应，甲硫氨酸的硫亲核进攻腺苷的 5′-碳，形成带正电的锍离子，三个磷酸全部离去。所以连接点是腺苷（含核糖）而不是游离腺嘌呤；不是与 ADP 缩合，SAM 分子里根本没有磷酸；也不是半胱氨酸——半胱氨酸出现在 SAM 下游的转硫途径末端，不在 SAM 本身。
quiz.explain_en: SAM is S-adenosylmethionine: ATP reacts with methionine, whose sulfur attacks the 5'-carbon of adenosine to form a positively charged sulfonium, with all three phosphates leaving. So the attachment is to adenosine, which includes the ribose, not to free adenine; it is not a condensation with ADP, since SAM contains no phosphate at all; and cysteine appears at the end of the downstream transsulfuration pathway, not in SAM itself.

quiz.q_zh: 胸腺嘧啶的分解与尿嘧啶的分解，关键差别在哪里？
quiz.q_en: Where does thymine's catabolism differ from uracil's?

options.zh: T 不经过还原，直接开环生成丙二酸半醛衍生物
options.en: T skips reduction; its ring opens to a semialdehyde

options.zh: T 的甲基先被 SAM 取走，再还原成饱和环
options.en: SAM removes T's methyl before the ring is reduced

options.zh: T 环上多一个甲基，终产物是 β-氨基异丁酸
options.en: T carries a methyl; it ends as β-aminoisobutyrate

options.zh: T 先脱氨基后，终产物与 U 同为 β-丙氨酸
options.en: T is deaminated first and ends as β-alanine too

quiz.explain_zh: T 与 U 的分解前两步完全平行（还原成二氢形式、开环水解），差别只在那个 5-甲基被一路带下来，所以终产物是 β-氨基异丁酸而不是 β-丙氨酸。T 环上没有氨基可脱；还原这一步 T 同样要走，不能跳过；SAM 是甲基供体不是甲基受体，不会把甲基从 T 上取走。
quiz.explain_en: The first two steps are exactly parallel for T and U (reduction to the dihydro form, then hydrolytic ring opening); the only difference is that the 5-methyl is carried all the way through, so the product is β-aminoisobutyrate rather than β-alanine. T has no amino group to remove; it does not skip the reduction step; and SAM is a methyl donor, not an acceptor, so it never strips the methyl off T.

title_zh: β-氨基异丁酸到琥珀酰CoA，以及碱基分解的三层次总结
title_en: β-aminoisobutyrate to succinyl-CoA, and the summary of base catabolism

points.zh: 他要求写下第二句结论：胸腺嘧啶代谢的最终产物是 β-氨基异丁酸。
points.en: He dictates the second take-home sentence: thymine metabolism ends at β-aminoisobutyrate.

points.zh: β-氨基异丁酸的最终去向是变成琥珀酰CoA，结构他说不用画，知道名字就行。
points.en: β-aminoisobutyrate ends up as succinyl-CoA; he says the structure need not be drawn as long as the name is known.

points.zh: 他明确声明：到这里只讲完了核苷酸「碱基的分解」这一部分。
points.en: He states explicitly that what has been covered so far is only the catabolism of the bases.

points.zh: 总结时他划掉了一句从教辅书上看来的话，说「我现在不确定这句话到底是不是对的」。
points.en: In summarising he crosses out one line he had taken from a study guide, saying he is no longer sure it is correct.

points.zh: 他唯一确定的是：嘌呤可以在碱基、核苷、核苷酸三种形式下发生代谢，三种形式的终产物都是尿酸。
points.en: The one thing he is sure of is that purines can be metabolised as base, as nucleoside and as nucleotide, and that all three routes end at uric acid.

points.zh: 嘧啶能不能在核苷和核苷酸层次代谢，他说不确定，教科书没讲，所以暂且当它不行。
points.en: Whether pyrimidines can be metabolised at the nucleoside and nucleotide levels he says he does not know, that the textbook did not say, so he provisionally treats it as impossible.

points.zh: 复述嘧啶的两条终点：胞嘧啶和尿嘧啶到 β-丙氨酸，掺入脂肪酸合成；胸腺嘧啶到 β-氨基异丁酸，再变琥珀酰CoA。
points.en: He restates the two pyrimidine endpoints: cytosine and uracil to β-alanine feeding fatty acid synthesis, and thymine to β-aminoisobutyrate and on to succinyl-CoA.

points.zh: 他的结论是嘧啶的产物可以汇入 TCA 循环，理由包括丙二酸单酰CoA「间接程度上也掺入了 TCA 循环」。
points.en: His conclusion is that pyrimidine products can feed the TCA cycle, arguing among other things that malonyl-CoA indirectly enters it too.

points.zh: 相对地，嘌呤的产物是直接排出的，所以他说人体对嘌呤的代谢「更弱」。
points.en: Purine products by contrast are excreted directly, which is why he calls the body's handling of purines weaker.

extra.zh: 丙二酸单酰CoA 不「间接汇入 TCA 循环」。它是脂肪酸合成的定向中间物，而且是 CPT-1 的抑制剂——它的存在恰恰是在阻断脂肪酸进线粒体氧化，是合成与氧化互斥的开关。嘧啶的碳真正进 TCA 的那条线是他自己讲对的另一条：胸腺嘧啶 → β-氨基异丁酸 → 甲基丙二酰CoA → 琥珀酰CoA。
extra.en: Malonyl-CoA does not indirectly feed the TCA cycle. It is a committed intermediate of fatty acid synthesis and an inhibitor of CPT-1 — its presence actively blocks fatty acids from entering mitochondria for oxidation, the switch that keeps synthesis and oxidation mutually exclusive. The line by which pyrimidine carbon genuinely reaches the TCA cycle is the other one he states correctly: thymine to β-aminoisobutyrate to methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA.

extra.zh: 嘧啶核苷酸的降解同样是从核苷酸开始的：先由核苷酸酶去磷酸，再由核苷磷酸化酶脱掉核糖，最后才在游离碱基上做还原和开环。所以「嘧啶只能在碱基水平代谢」的结论偏保守；准确的说法是环的化学改造只发生在碱基上，但脱磷酸和脱糖这两步跟嘌呤一样。他标注不确定并划掉，这个处理本身是诚实且值得学的。
extra.en: Pyrimidine nucleotides are degraded starting from the nucleotide as well: a nucleotidase removes the phosphate, a nucleoside phosphorylase removes the ribose, and only then is the free base reduced and ring-opened. So the conclusion that pyrimidines are handled only at the base level is too conservative; more precisely, the chemical remodelling of the ring happens only on the base, but the dephosphorylation and desugaring steps are the same as for purines. Marking the point as uncertain and crossing it out was, in itself, the honest thing to do.

extra.zh: β-氨基异丁酸到琥珀酰CoA 的中间步值得知道：转氨成甲基丙二酸半醛 → 丙酰CoA → 甲基丙二酰CoA →（甲基丙二酰CoA 变位酶，维生素 B12 依赖）→ 琥珀酰CoA。这条路与奇数碳脂肪酸、缬氨酸/异亮氨酸/苏氨酸/甲硫氨酸的碳骨架共用同一个出口，B12 缺乏时甲基丙二酸会堆积——这是临床上测甲基丙二酸判断 B12 状态的依据。
extra.en: The intermediate steps from β-aminoisobutyrate to succinyl-CoA are worth knowing: transamination to methylmalonate semialdehyde, then propionyl-CoA, then methylmalonyl-CoA, then succinyl-CoA via the B12-dependent methylmalonyl-CoA mutase. This exit is shared with odd-chain fatty acids and the carbon skeletons of valine, isoleucine, threonine and methionine, and methylmalonate accumulates when B12 is deficient — the basis for measuring it clinically.

extra.zh: 两类碱基「可利用/不可利用」的真正分界在氮上：嘧啶环开环后释放 NH3 和 CO2，这部分氮进尿素循环，碳骨架留下来做 β-丙氨酸或 β-氨基异丁酸；嘌呤环的四个氮全部保留在尿酸分子里，随尿原样排掉，一个都收不回来。所以嘌呤分解的净收益接近于零。
extra.en: The real dividing line between the two base classes lies in the nitrogen: opening the pyrimidine ring releases NH3 and CO2, that nitrogen enters the urea cycle, and the carbon skeleton remains as β-alanine or β-aminoisobutyrate. All four nitrogens of the purine ring stay in the uric acid molecule and are excreted unchanged, none of them recovered. The net return from purine catabolism is therefore close to nothing.

quiz.q_zh: 嘧啶的碳骨架真正汇入 TCA 循环走的是哪条路？
quiz.q_en: By which route does pyrimidine carbon genuinely reach the TCA cycle?

options.zh: β-丙氨酸先变成丙二酸单酰CoA，再直接进入循环
options.en: β-alanine becomes malonyl-CoA and enters the cycle

options.zh: β-丙氨酸经转氨后以草酰乙酸形式补入循环
options.en: β-alanine is transaminated into oxaloacetate first

options.zh: β-氨基异丁酸经甲基丙二酰CoA 到琥珀酰CoA
options.en: β-aminoisobutyrate goes through methylmalonyl-CoA

options.zh: 尿酸开环之后以延胡索酸的形式直接补入该循环
options.en: Uric acid opens up and feeds in as fumarate here

quiz.explain_zh: T 的碳经 β-氨基异丁酸 → 甲基丙二酸半醛 → 丙酰CoA → 甲基丙二酰CoA → 琥珀酰CoA，琥珀酰CoA 就是 TCA 循环的成员。丙二酸单酰CoA 是脂肪酸合成的定向中间物、还抑制 CPT-1，它不进 TCA；β-丙氨酸不生成草酰乙酸；尿酸在人体内根本不开环，直接随尿排出。
quiz.explain_en: Thymine carbon runs β-aminoisobutyrate to methylmalonate semialdehyde to propionyl-CoA to methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA, and succinyl-CoA is a cycle member. Malonyl-CoA is a committed fatty-acid-synthesis intermediate that also inhibits CPT-1, and it does not enter the cycle; β-alanine does not give oxaloacetate; and uric acid is never ring-opened in humans, being excreted intact.

quiz.q_zh: 关于嘌呤分解可以发生在哪些层次，正确的说法是什么？
quiz.q_en: At which levels can purine catabolism take place?

options.zh: 碱基、核苷、核苷酸三个层次都可以，终点都是尿酸
options.en: Base, nucleoside and nucleotide all work; urate ends it

options.zh: 只能在游离碱基这一个层次上进行，先脱磷酸再脱核糖
options.en: Only free bases, after phosphate and ribose come off

options.zh: 只能在核苷酸层次进行，脱氨与去磷酸同时发生
options.en: Only nucleotides, with deamination and dephosphorylation

options.zh: 只在核苷层次进行，磷酸必须先由核苷酸酶除去
options.en: Only nucleosides, once nucleotidase removes phosphate

quiz.explain_zh: 这是他明确说自己唯一确定的一句：脱氨可以发生在核苷酸（AMP 脱氨酶）、核苷（腺苷脱氨酶 ADA）和碱基三个层次上，三条路都汇到次黄嘌呤核苷或次黄嘌呤，终点都是尿酸。说只能在游离碱基、只能在核苷酸、只在核苷层次进行的三种表述，各自排除了另外两个层次上确实存在的酶。
quiz.explain_en: This is the one point he says he is certain of: deamination happens at the nucleotide level (AMP deaminase), the nucleoside level (adenosine deaminase, ADA) and the base level, all three converging on inosine or hypoxanthine and ending at uric acid. Restricting it to free bases only, to nucleotides only, or to nucleosides only each rules out enzymes that demonstrably act at the other levels.

title_zh: 尿酸难溶与痛风的成因，转入核苷酸的合成
title_en: Poorly soluble urate, gout, and the turn towards nucleotide synthesis

points.zh: 他说尿酸的溶解度没有那么高，所以对人体没有什么利用价值，这是嘌呤产物直接排出的原因。
points.en: He notes that uric acid is not very soluble and therefore of no use to the body, which is why purine products are simply excreted.

points.zh: 他举例：假设吃一公斤牛肉、牛肉里 ATCG 各占 25%。
points.en: He offers an example: eating one kilogram of beef, assuming A, T, C and G each make up 25%.

points.zh: 他说其中的 C 和 T 这两个嘧啶人可以完全利用起来，变到 TCA 循环里去。
points.en: He says the two pyrimidines, C and T, can be fully used and routed into the TCA cycle.

points.zh: 他说剩下的「那 500 克嘌呤」人没有办法利用起来。
points.en: He says the remaining 500 grams of purine cannot be used at all.

points.zh: 他说唯独嘌呤的分解代谢有一个速度上限，所以人很容易得痛风。
points.en: He says purine catabolism uniquely has a speed ceiling, which is why gout is so easy to develop.

points.zh: 他补充现在生活太好、人吃得多，所以不一定是喝嘌呤汤引起的，跟食物总量关系很大。
points.en: He adds that modern diets are simply too rich, so it is not necessarily the purine-heavy soup, and total food intake matters a great deal.

points.zh: 分解讲完，转入合成：他说整个代谢大板块里唯一比较重要的合成就是核苷酸的合成，脂肪酸合成都没那么重要。
points.en: With catabolism finished he turns to synthesis, saying that in the whole metabolism block the one synthesis that matters is nucleotide synthesis, more even than fatty acid synthesis.

points.zh: 他明确 NT 在他的板书里指的都是核苷酸，即带核糖和磷酸的形式。
points.en: He states that NT on his board always means nucleotide, the form carrying both ribose and phosphate.

points.zh: 任意核苷酸的生物合成主要有两种形式：从头合成和补救合成；从头合成的定义是不以现成的碱基为原料，从二氧化碳、一碳单位这种最小单元开始一点一点构筑。
points.en: Any nucleotide can be made two ways, de novo and salvage; de novo he defines as not using a ready-made base but building up piece by piece from the smallest units such as carbon dioxide and one-carbon groups.

extra.zh: 「一公斤牛肉里 500 克嘌呤」这个数字必须划掉。ATCG 各 25% 说的是碱基组成的摩尔比例，不是牛肉的质量比例——肌肉里核酸的质量占比远低于 1%，一公斤牛肉里的嘌呤是克级甚至更低。他要讲的道理（嘌呤那一半回收不了）是对的，数字给得太具体，很容易被当成事实背下来。
extra.en: The figure of 500 g of purine per kilogram of beef has to go. A, T, C and G at 25% each describes the molar base composition, not the mass fraction of the meat — nucleic acid is well under 1% of muscle by mass, so a kilogram of beef contains on the order of grams of purine at most. The point he is making (that half of it cannot be recovered) is sound; the number is specific enough to be memorised as fact.

extra.zh: 人容易痛风的主因不是「分解速度有上限」，而是两点：一，人缺尿酸酶，代谢在尿酸这一步就停了，没有下游可以泄压；二，肾脏对尿酸的净排泄能力有限（近端小管重吸收约 90%，URAT1 等转运体主导），限速在排泄端而不是分解端。这也是为什么降尿酸药分两类：抑制生成的别嘌呤醇/非布司他，和促进排泄的苯溴马隆/丙磺舒。
extra.en: The main reason humans get gout is not a ceiling on the rate of breakdown but two other things: humans lack uricase, so metabolism stops at urate with no downstream relief valve; and renal net excretion of urate is limited, with about 90% reabsorbed in the proximal tubule mainly via URAT1 and related transporters. The bottleneck is at excretion, not at degradation. This is why urate-lowering drugs come in two classes: allopurinol and febuxostat, which reduce production, and benzbromarone and probenecid, which promote excretion.

extra.zh: 尿酸难溶是有具体数字的：37 °C 血浆中单钠尿酸盐的溶解上限约 6.8 mg/dL，超过这个浓度就可能析出针状结晶，这正是临床把治疗靶标定在血尿酸 < 6 mg/dL 的来源。结晶沉积在温度较低、pH 较低的远端关节（第一跖趾关节最典型），被巨噬细胞吞噬后激活 NLRP3 炎症小体、释放 IL-1β，这才是痛风急性发作的机制。
extra.en: The insolubility of urate has a number attached: monosodium urate saturates plasma at about 6.8 mg/dL at 37 °C, above which needle-shaped crystals can form — the origin of the clinical target of keeping serum urate below 6 mg/dL. Crystals deposit in cooler, more acidic distal joints, classically the first metatarsophalangeal, and once phagocytosed by macrophages they activate the NLRP3 inflammasome and release IL-1β, which is what an acute gout attack actually is.

extra.zh: 从头合成 de novo 和补救合成 salvage 的分界不是「快慢」，而是起点：de novo 从 PRPP 和小分子原料造出一个全新的环，salvage 用的是已经存在的碱基或核苷。快慢是结果不是定义。另外补救途径在某些组织里不是备用而是主力——脑和骨髓几乎不做嘌呤从头合成，只能靠补救，HGPRT 缺陷造成 Lesch-Nyhan 综合征的神经症状正源于此。
extra.en: What separates de novo from salvage is not speed but starting material: de novo builds a brand-new ring from PRPP and small precursors, salvage reuses an existing base or nucleoside. The speed difference is a consequence, not the definition. And in some tissues salvage is not a backup but the main route — brain and bone marrow carry out almost no de novo purine synthesis and depend on salvage, which is why HGPRT deficiency produces the neurological picture of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.

quiz.q_zh: 人比其他多数哺乳动物更容易得痛风，最根本的原因是什么？
quiz.q_en: Why are humans more prone to gout than most other mammals?

options.zh: 人缺尿酸酶，代谢停在难溶的尿酸且排泄有限
options.en: No uricase: it stops at poorly soluble urate

options.zh: 嘌呤分解代谢的速度上限低于嘧啶的分解速度上限
options.en: Purine breakdown runs at a lower speed ceiling

options.zh: 人的黄嘌呤氧化酶活性远高于其他哺乳动物
options.en: Human xanthine oxidase is far more active

options.zh: 食物中嘌呤的质量占比高达碱基总量的一半
options.en: Purines make up half the mass of any meat

quiz.explain_zh: 灵长类的尿酸酶基因假基因化，代谢在尿酸这一步就没有下游了，加上肾小管把滤过的尿酸重吸收约九成，血尿酸容易超过 6.8 mg/dL 的溶解上限而结晶。分解速度上限不是主因；人的 XO 活性并不特别高，活性高反而只是把底物更快推到同一个终点；而「嘌呤占食物质量一半」是老师那个 500 克例子里被放大的数字，核酸在肌肉里的质量占比不到 1%。
quiz.explain_en: The uricase gene is a pseudogene in primates, so metabolism has nowhere to go past urate, and the renal tubule reabsorbs about 90% of filtered urate, so serum levels readily exceed the 6.8 mg/dL solubility limit and crystallise. A ceiling on degradation rate is not the driver; human XO is not unusually active, and higher activity would only push substrate faster to the same endpoint; and purines being half the mass of food is the inflated figure from his 500-gram example, since nucleic acid is under 1% of muscle by mass.

quiz.q_zh: 老师说一公斤牛肉里有 500 克嘌呤，问题出在哪里？
quiz.q_en: What is wrong with the claim that a kilogram of beef contains 500 g of purine?

options.zh: 牛肉中的嘌呤大部分已以尿酸形式存在
options.en: Most beef purine is already there as urate

options.zh: 牛肉的核酸含量应当按干重而不是湿重算
options.en: Nucleic acid should be counted on dry weight

options.zh: 牛肉里 A 和 G 的比例远低于 25%
options.en: A and G sit well below 25% in real beef

options.zh: 25% 说的是碱基的组成比例，不是质量占比
options.en: 25% describes base composition, not mass

quiz.explain_zh: ATCG 各 25% 描述的是核酸内部碱基的组成比例，跟牛肉整体的质量分布是两个层级的量。肌肉组织里核酸的质量占比远低于百分之一，所以一公斤牛肉里的嘌呤是克级。牛肉中 A 和 G 的比例大致就是接近一半（嘌呤对嘧啶），并不特别低；牛肉里的嘌呤以核酸和游离核苷酸为主而不是尿酸；干重湿重之分只会改变一个小系数，救不回三个数量级的差距。
quiz.explain_en: A, T, C and G at 25% each describes composition within the nucleic acid, a completely different level of quantity from the mass breakdown of the meat. Nucleic acid is well under one percent of muscle by mass, so a kilogram of beef holds purine on the order of grams. The proportion of A and G in beef is in fact around half of the bases, not unusually low; beef purine exists mostly as nucleic acid and free nucleotides rather than urate; and switching between wet and dry weight changes a small factor, nowhere near the three orders of magnitude involved.

title_zh: 从头合成与补救合成的定义（关键更正），嘌呤环的第一块拼图
title_en: De novo versus salvage as he defines them (key correction), and the first piece of the purine ring

points.zh: 他把从头合成描述成：从二氧化碳、一碳单位这种最小单元开始，一点一点构筑起需要的碱基，把碱基加到核糖上，核糖再接受一分子磷酸，最终变成核苷酸。
points.en: He describes de novo synthesis as starting from the smallest units such as carbon dioxide and one-carbon groups, building up the required base bit by bit, attaching the base to ribose, and having the ribose then take on a phosphate to become a nucleotide.

points.zh: 补救合成他用组织损伤来引入：某块组织受了严重创伤、被细菌弄死了一大片，机体需要尽快修复。
points.en: He introduces salvage with tissue damage: a patch of tissue badly injured or wiped out by bacteria, which the body needs to repair fast.

points.zh: 他给的对比是从头合成过程比较慢，补救合成是一种比较快的方式。
points.en: His contrast is that de novo is fairly slow while salvage is the fast option.

points.zh: 补救合成直接利用体内游离的嘌呤和核苷。
points.en: Salvage directly uses the free purines and nucleosides already present in the body.

points.zh: 他说这些游离嘌呤和核苷可以来自吃饭：食物核苷酸被降解以后，总会有一些还来不及被进一步分解的游离碱基和核苷。
points.en: He says these free purines and nucleosides can come from food: once dietary nucleotides are degraded, some free bases and nucleosides remain before further breakdown catches up.

points.zh: 他强调补救合成的限制：如果你没有现成的核苷、嘌呤和嘧啶，就走不了补救路线。
points.en: He stresses the limitation of salvage: with no ready-made nucleoside, purine or pyrimidine on hand, the route is unavailable.

points.zh: 转入嘌呤的从头合成，他用红框框起来，并说不去详细讲它到底怎么合成。
points.en: He turns to purine de novo synthesis, boxes it in red, and says he will not go through how the synthesis actually proceeds.

points.zh: 要求掌握的是：嘌呤这个环上每一个原子来源于什么；他把这个环称作「这是个六元环」。
points.en: What must be known is where each atom of the purine ring comes from; he refers to the ring as a six-membered ring.

points.zh: 第一块拼图是一分子甘氨酸。他在旁边画甘氨酸的结构，说成「这里是个羧基 COOH，这里是个 NH2，然后这里是个甲基」。
points.en: The first piece is one molecule of glycine. He draws its structure beside the ring, describing it as a carboxyl COOH, an NH2, and a methyl group.

extra.zh: 本段最要紧的一条：嘌呤从头合成的方向被讲反了。他说的「先构筑起碱基，再加到核糖上，核糖再接一分子磷酸」是嘧啶的路线——嘧啶确实先造环（氨甲酰磷酸 + 天冬氨酸 → 乳清酸），再接上 PRPP 得到 OMP，脱羧成 UMP。嘌呤正相反：嘌呤环是直接在 PRPP 上一步步搭起来的。PRPP 先与谷氨酰胺反应生成 5-磷酸核糖胺（那个氮就是将来的 N9），此后甘氨酸、甲酰基、谷氨酰胺、天冬氨酸、CO2 每一个原子都加在这个已经带着核糖和磷酸的骨架上，第 10 步才闭环成 IMP。所以嘌呤合成过程中从来不存在一个游离碱基去「加到核糖上」，磷酸也不是最后才接的，一开始就在（PRPP = 5-磷酸核糖-1-焦磷酸）。他接下来讲环上原子来源时也完全没有提 PRPP，本段范围内没有自我更正。
extra.en: The most important correction here: the direction of purine de novo synthesis is reversed. What he describes — build the base, attach it to ribose, then phosphorylate — is the pyrimidine route, where the ring really is made first (carbamoyl phosphate plus aspartate to orotate) and then joined to PRPP to give OMP, decarboxylated to UMP. Purines work the opposite way: the ring is assembled step by step directly on PRPP. PRPP first reacts with glutamine to give 5-phosphoribosylamine, whose nitrogen becomes N9, and every subsequent atom — glycine, formyl groups, glutamine, aspartate, CO2 — is added onto a scaffold that already carries ribose and phosphate, with ring closure to IMP only at step ten. So no free base is ever attached to ribose during purine synthesis, and the phosphate is not added last but present from the outset (PRPP = 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate). He also omits PRPP entirely when he goes on to list where the ring atoms come from, and does not correct himself within this stretch.

extra.zh: 甘氨酸没有甲基。它的侧链就是一个氢原子，中间那个碳是 α-碳，上面连着 COOH、NH2 和两个 H，是亚甲基 CH2。这个细节在下一分钟会变得重要：正因为甘氨酸只有两个碳，它整分子掺入嘌呤环时刚好给出 C4 和 C5 两个碳加 N7 一个氮。
extra.en: Glycine has no methyl group. Its side chain is a single hydrogen; the central carbon is the α-carbon bearing COOH, NH2 and two hydrogens, i.e. a CH2. This detail matters within the next minute: precisely because glycine has only two carbons, incorporating the whole molecule into the purine ring supplies exactly C4 and C5 plus the nitrogen N7.

extra.zh: 从头合成的限速步和调控点是谷氨酰胺-PRPP 酰胺转移酶（GPAT），即 PRPP + 谷氨酰胺 → 5-磷酸核糖胺 那一步，它被终产物 AMP、GMP、IMP 反馈抑制、被 PRPP 前馈激活。整条从头合成造一个 IMP 要消耗 5 个 ATP 当量，比补救途径的一步一个 PRPP 昂贵得多——这才是「从头合成慢」背后真正的能量账。
extra.en: The committed, regulated step of de novo synthesis is glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase (GPAT), the reaction PRPP plus glutamine to 5-phosphoribosylamine, feedback-inhibited by the end products AMP, GMP and IMP and feed-forward activated by PRPP. Building one IMP de novo costs about five ATP equivalents, far more than the single PRPP consumed by a one-step salvage reaction — this is the real energy accounting behind de novo being the slow route.

extra.zh: 嘌呤和嘧啶从头合成还有一个方向上的对称差别值得一起记：嘌呤是「先有糖，后有环」，嘧啶是「先有环，后有糖」，但两条路都要用到 PRPP，只是用在不同的时间点。记法可以是：嘌呤把 PRPP 当地基，嘧啶把 PRPP 当底座后装。
extra.en: There is a symmetric contrast worth learning as a pair: purines are sugar first, ring second; pyrimidines are ring first, sugar second. Both routes use PRPP, but at different moments. One way to hold it: purines treat PRPP as the foundation they build on, pyrimidines bolt PRPP on as a base at the end.

quiz.q_zh: 嘌呤环的从头合成是按什么顺序进行的？
quiz.q_en: In what order is the purine ring assembled de novo?

options.zh: 先造出核糖-1-磷酸，再把碱基接到它的 1 位上
options.en: Ribose-1-phosphate forms first, then takes the base

options.zh: 先合成乳清酸环，再与 PRPP 缩合并脱羧成 IMP
options.en: Orotate is made first, then joined onto the PRPP

options.zh: 环从 PRPP 上的氨基逐个原子搭起，闭环成 IMP
options.en: Atom by atom on PRPP, closing at last into IMP

options.zh: 先拼出完整的嘌呤碱基，再接到核糖上并加上磷酸
options.en: The free base is built first, then put on ribose

quiz.explain_zh: 嘌呤从头合成从 PRPP 出发，先由谷氨酰胺提供氮生成 5-磷酸核糖胺，此后每一个原子都加在已经带着核糖和磷酸的骨架上，第 10 步闭环得到 IMP。先造出完整碱基再接到核糖上、磷酸最后才接，正是老师讲错的那条路；核糖-1-磷酸参与的是核苷磷酸化酶的可逆反应而不是从头合成；先造乳清酸环再接 PRPP 是嘧啶的路线，而且产物是 UMP 不是 IMP。
quiz.explain_en: Purine de novo synthesis starts from PRPP: glutamine donates the nitrogen to give 5-phosphoribosylamine, and every atom thereafter is added onto a scaffold that already carries ribose and phosphate, with ring closure to IMP at step ten. Building the complete base first and attaching it to ribose with the phosphate added last is exactly the error in the lecture; ribose-1-phosphate belongs to the reversible nucleoside phosphorylase reaction, not to de novo synthesis; and making orotate first and then joining PRPP is the pyrimidine route, whose product is UMP rather than IMP.

quiz.q_zh: 补救合成之所以比从头合成快，直接原因是什么？
quiz.q_en: What directly makes salvage faster than de novo synthesis?

options.zh: 它跳过 IMP，同时生成 AMP 与 GMP
options.en: It skips IMP and yields both AMP and GMP at once

options.zh: 它由 ATP 直接供能，不需要任何辅酶参与
options.en: ATP powers it directly and no cofactor is needed

options.zh: 它在线粒体内进行，那里的底物浓度高很多
options.en: It runs in mitochondria where substrates pile up

options.zh: 它直接用现成的游离碱基一步接到 PRPP 上
options.en: A ready-made base is joined to PRPP in one step

quiz.explain_zh: 补救途径由 APRT 或 HGPRT 一步把现成碱基接到 PRPP 上生成单磷酸核苷酸，一步对上从头合成的十步，能量代价也从约 5 个 ATP 当量降到一个 PRPP。它不是靠 ATP 直接供能的特殊供能方式；它发生在胞质而不是线粒体；HGPRT 的产物恰恰包括 IMP，谈不上跳过 IMP。
quiz.explain_en: Salvage uses APRT or HGPRT to join a ready-made base to PRPP in a single step, giving a nucleoside monophosphate — one step against ten, and an energy cost falling from roughly five ATP equivalents to one PRPP. It is not powered by any special direct use of ATP; it takes place in the cytosol rather than mitochondria; and HGPRT's products actually include IMP, so nothing is skipped.

quiz.q_zh: 嘧啶的从头合成在顺序上与嘌呤有什么不同？
quiz.q_en: How does pyrimidine de novo synthesis differ in order from purine?

options.zh: 嘧啶从游离的核糖开始，磷酸在最后一步接上
options.en: It starts on free ribose; phosphate is added last

options.zh: 嘧啶先造乳清酸环，之后接上 PRPP 成 OMP
options.en: Orotate is built first, then PRPP gives OMP

options.zh: 嘧啶同样在 PRPP 上逐个原子搭建整个环系
options.en: Pyrimidines are also assembled atom-wise on PRPP

options.zh: 嘧啶环先接上核糖，再由 CO2 补上最后一个碳
options.en: The ring takes ribose first, then CO2 adds a carbon

quiz.explain_zh: 嘧啶走的是先造环后接糖：氨甲酰磷酸与天冬氨酸缩合、环化、氧化得到乳清酸，乳清酸再与 PRPP 反应生成 OMP，脱羧成 UMP。在 PRPP 上逐个原子搭建整个环系说的是嘌呤；CO2 补最后一个碳是嘌呤 C6 的来源，不是嘧啶的收尾步；从游离核糖开始、磷酸最后接上这两条在任何一条从头合成里都不成立，因为糖始终是以 PRPP 的形式进来的。
quiz.explain_en: Pyrimidines go ring first, sugar second: carbamoyl phosphate condenses with aspartate, cyclises and is oxidised to orotate, which then reacts with PRPP to give OMP and is decarboxylated to UMP. Assembling the whole ring atom by atom on PRPP describes purines; CO2 supplying a final carbon is the origin of purine C6, not a pyrimidine finishing step; and starting from free ribose with phosphate added last is false for either pathway, since the sugar always enters as PRPP.

title_zh: 嘌呤环上每一个原子的来源
title_en: Where every atom of the purine ring comes from

points.zh: 他先定位甘氨酸：环上 4、5、7 这三个位置来自一分子甘氨酸。
points.en: He places glycine first: positions 4, 5 and 7 of the ring come from one molecule of glycine.

points.zh: 但他补了一句说甘氨酸「经过了一个脱羧，把这边的羧基脱掉了」。
points.en: He adds, however, that the glycine has been decarboxylated, with the carboxyl group removed.

points.zh: 接着从小环讲起：小环下边的 8 位是一个一碳单位，由四氢叶酸供给。
points.en: He then starts with the small ring: position 8 at its bottom is a one-carbon unit supplied by tetrahydrofolate.

points.zh: 小环下边的那个氮（9 位）由谷氨酰胺供给，理由是谷氨酰胺是游离氨基的载体。
points.en: The nitrogen at the bottom of the small ring, N9, comes from glutamine, on the grounds that glutamine carries free amino nitrogen.

points.zh: 他指出左边是对称的、比较好记：两个一碳单位都由四氢叶酸供给，两个氮都由谷氨酰胺的游离氮供给。
points.en: He points out a symmetry on the left that makes it easy to remember: both one-carbon units come from tetrahydrofolate and both nitrogens from glutamine's free nitrogen.

points.zh: 他说最恶心的是左上角的 1 位氮，它由天冬氨酸供给，因为天冬氨酸也是游离氨的一种承载体。
points.en: He calls the nitrogen at top left, N1, the nastiest one: it comes from aspartate, since aspartate is another carrier of free amino nitrogen.

points.zh: 最上面的那个碳（6 位）由二氧化碳供给。
points.en: The carbon at the top, C6, is supplied by carbon dioxide.

points.zh: 总结成「三四部分」：第一个甘氨酸、第二个两个一碳单位、第三个两个谷氨酰胺、第四个一个天冬氨酸。
points.en: He sums it up as three or four parts: glycine first, then two one-carbon units, then two glutamines, then one aspartate.

points.zh: 学生追问一碳单位是什么，他答「它就是一个 CH3 游离的甲基」，随即改口说也不是游离的，主要是从四氢叶酸来的。
points.en: Asked what a one-carbon unit is, he answers that it is a CH3, a free methyl group, then corrects himself to say not free, and that it comes mainly from tetrahydrofolate.

extra.zh: 甘氨酸没有脱羧。他前一句「4、5、7 三位是一个甘氨酸」是对的，而这正好否定了脱羧：甘氨酸是整分子掺入的，氮 → N7、α-碳 → C5、羧基碳 → C4，三个原子全部用上。机制上 GAR 合成酶就是用甘氨酸的羧基与 5-磷酸核糖胺的氨基缩合成酰胺键，羧基碳被保留在环里。如果真脱了羧，C4 就没有来源了。
extra.en: Glycine is not decarboxylated. His preceding sentence — that positions 4, 5 and 7 come from one glycine — is correct, and it rules the decarboxylation out: the whole molecule is incorporated, nitrogen to N7, α-carbon to C5, carboxyl carbon to C4, all three atoms used. Mechanistically GAR synthetase condenses the glycine carboxyl with the amino group of 5-phosphoribosylamine into an amide bond, keeping that carbon in the ring. Had the carboxyl been lost, C4 would have no source at all.

extra.zh: 一碳单位不是甲基。四氢叶酸携带的一碳单位有多个氧化态，嘌呤环 C2 和 C8 用的是甲酰基 formyl（甲酸的氧化态），供体是 N10-甲酰四氢叶酸，由 GAR 转甲酰酶和 AICAR 转甲酰酶两个酶分别加上去。甲基那一档（N5-甲基四氢叶酸 → 甲硫氨酸 → SAM）是叶酸一碳单位的另一条去向；他自己在这里拿含硫的 SAM 做类比，恰好说明两者不是一回事。说成 CH3 会让人以为 C8 上挂着一个甲基。
extra.en: A one-carbon unit is not a methyl group. Tetrahydrofolate carries one-carbon units at several oxidation states, and purine C2 and C8 use the formyl level (the oxidation state of formate), donated by N10-formyl tetrahydrofolate and installed by GAR transformylase and AICAR transformylase respectively. The methyl level (N5-methyl THF to methionine to SAM) is a separate fate of folate one-carbon units; his own analogy to the sulfur-containing SAM shows the two are not the same. Calling it CH3 suggests a methyl group hanging off C8, which there is not.

extra.zh: 他的「三四部分」清单漏了 CO2 提供 C6——虽然他上一句刚讲过。完整的五个来源是：甘氨酸（C4、C5、N7）、谷氨酰胺酰胺氮（N3、N9）、天冬氨酸（N1）、N10-甲酰四氢叶酸（C2、C8）、CO2（C6），加起来正好 9 个环原子。记忆上可以按「一个氨基酸整分子进（甘氨酸）、两个氨基酸只给氮（谷氨酰胺给两个、天冬氨酸给一个）、两个碳来自叶酸、一个碳来自 CO2」。
extra.en: His list of three or four parts omits CO2 supplying C6, even though he had just said so a sentence earlier. The complete set of five sources is: glycine (C4, C5, N7), glutamine amide nitrogen (N3, N9), aspartate (N1), N10-formyl tetrahydrofolate (C2, C8) and CO2 (C6) — exactly the nine ring atoms. A way to hold it: one amino acid enters whole (glycine), two donate only nitrogen (glutamine twice, aspartate once), two carbons come from folate and one from CO2.

extra.zh: 这里的两个氮供体分工，正好和嘌呤降解的临床落点相扣：磺胺类药物阻断细菌自己合成叶酸，一碳单位断供，C2 和 C8 加不上，嘌呤从头合成停摆——这就是为什么磺胺对人无毒（人不能合成叶酸、只能吃进来，没有这个靶点）。甲氨蝶呤走的是同一条逻辑的另一端：抑制 DHFR，把已有的叶酸锁在二氢态，同样断掉 C2/C8 与 dTMP。
extra.en: The division of labour among the nitrogen donors here connects directly to the clinical end of this pathway: sulfonamides block bacterial folate synthesis, cutting off one-carbon units so that C2 and C8 cannot be added and purine de novo synthesis stalls — which is why sulfonamides are non-toxic to humans, who cannot make folate and must eat it, and so lack the target. Methotrexate attacks the same logic from the other side, inhibiting DHFR so existing folate is trapped in the dihydro state, again cutting off C2, C8 and dTMP.

quiz.q_zh: 甘氨酸整分子掺入嘌呤环时贡献的是哪几个位置？
quiz.q_en: Which positions does glycine contribute when it enters the purine ring whole?

options.zh: 只贡献 N7，它的羧基碳在成环前被脱羧除去
options.en: Only N7, the carboxyl carbon being removed first

options.zh: 贡献 C4、C5 和 N7 三个原子，羧基碳保留
options.en: C4, C5 and N7, with the carboxyl carbon retained

options.zh: 贡献 C2、C8 两个碳，氮由谷氨酰胺提供
options.en: C2 and C8, while glutamine supplies the nitrogen

options.zh: 贡献 N1 和 N3，碳骨架进入嘧啶环的一侧
options.en: N1 and N3, its carbons entering the six-ring side

quiz.explain_zh: 甘氨酸只有两个碳一个氮，整分子掺入刚好给出 C4（羧基碳）、C5（α-碳）和 N7，GAR 合成酶用的正是它的羧基去成酰胺键，所以不存在脱羧。C2 和 C8 是 N10-甲酰四氢叶酸给的甲酰碳；N1 由天冬氨酸给、N3 由谷氨酰胺给，都不是甘氨酸的贡献。
quiz.explain_en: Glycine has just two carbons and one nitrogen, and incorporating it whole yields exactly C4 (the carboxyl carbon), C5 (the α-carbon) and N7; GAR synthetase uses that very carboxyl to form the amide bond, so no decarboxylation occurs. C2 and C8 are formyl carbons from N10-formyl tetrahydrofolate, while N1 comes from aspartate and N3 from glutamine — none of them glycine's doing.

quiz.q_zh: 嘌呤环 C2 和 C8 上接的一碳单位处于什么氧化态，由谁提供？
quiz.q_en: At what oxidation state are the one-carbon units at purine C2 and C8, and who donates them?

options.zh: 甲酸根，由游离的甲酸直接与嘌呤环缩合
options.en: Formate, condensing onto the ring from solution

options.zh: 甲酰基，其供体是 N10-甲酰四氢叶酸分子
options.en: Formyl, donated by N10-formyl tetrahydrofolate

options.zh: 甲基，其供体为 N5-甲基四氢叶酸分子
options.en: Methyl, donated by N5-methyl tetrahydrofolate

options.zh: 亚甲基，供体是 N5,N10-亚甲基四氢叶酸
options.en: Methylene, from N5,N10-methylene tetrahydrofolate

quiz.explain_zh: C2 和 C8 由 N10-甲酰四氢叶酸提供甲酰基，分别由 GAR 转甲酰酶和 AICAR 转甲酰酶催化。N5-甲基四氢叶酸的甲基去向是甲硫氨酸再到 SAM，不进嘌呤环；N5,N10-亚甲基四氢叶酸的去向是胸苷酸合酶把 dUMP 变 dTMP；游离甲酸不能直接缩合上环，必须先被四氢叶酸捕获成甲酰形式。
quiz.explain_en: C2 and C8 receive formyl groups from N10-formyl tetrahydrofolate, installed by GAR transformylase and AICAR transformylase respectively. The methyl of N5-methyl THF goes to methionine and then SAM and never enters the purine ring; N5,N10-methylene THF goes to thymidylate synthase converting dUMP to dTMP; and free formate cannot condense onto the ring directly, having first to be captured by tetrahydrofolate as a formyl group.

quiz.q_zh: 嘌呤环上 N1 和 C6 分别由什么提供？
quiz.q_en: What supplies N1 and C6 of the purine ring?

options.zh: N1 由甘氨酸提供，C6 由四氢叶酸提供甲酰
options.en: Glycine gives N1 and folate formyl gives C6

options.zh: N1 由天冬氨酸提供，C6 由二氧化碳提供
options.en: Aspartate gives N1 and carbon dioxide gives C6

options.zh: N1 由游离氨提供，C6 由甲硫氨酸的甲基提供
options.en: Free ammonia gives N1; SAM methyl gives C6

options.zh: N1 由谷氨酰胺提供，C6 由一碳单位提供
options.en: Glutamine gives N1; a one-carbon unit gives C6

quiz.explain_zh: N1 由天冬氨酸提供，机制与尿素循环第三步同型：天冬氨酸先与环缩合，再由裂解酶以延胡索酸的形式把碳骨架释放掉，只留下氮。C6 由 CO2（实际是 HCO3-）羧化 AIR 而来。谷氨酰胺给的是 N3 和 N9，甘氨酸给的是 C4、C5、N7，四氢叶酸的甲酰基给的是 C2 和 C8，甲硫氨酸的甲基完全不参与嘌呤环。
